tittel: Enhancing Students Academic Performance Using Organization Development Interventions (ODI): A Case Study of Business Management Major Students in Zhejiang Yuexiu University in China
kilde: ABAC ODI JOURNAL Vision. Action. Outcome
sammendrag: In recent years, the enrollment scale of the Business Administration major within the School of Applied Foreign Languages (SAFL) at Zhejiang Yuexiu University (ZYU) has grown year by year. As a higher vocational college, this school primarily enrolls students from Zhejiang Province, China. The students comprise graduates from both regular senior high schools and vocational high schools, with the latter accounting for a larger proportion. Vocational high school graduates often have a weaker foundation in basic knowledge, and their learning initiative, academic attitudes, and academic performance require improvement. Against this background, this study selected 40 sophomore students (vocational high school graduates) from the Department of Business Management as the research subjects, aiming to explore how to enhance their academic performance through Organizational Development Interventions (ODI). This study adopted quantitative and qualitative methods, utilizing questionnaire surveys and interviews as primary research instruments. Identical questionnaires and interview protocols were administered at different stages to collect data and assess outcomes, allowing for a comparison between pre-ODI and post-ODI conditions. Quantitative data analysis revealed statistically significant differences in all measured variables before and after the intervention, specifically in student motivation, student engagement, academic self-concept, self-efficacy, and academic performance. Furthermore, both quantitative and qualitative data indicate that the following instructional interventions—Appreciative Inquiry (AI), team building, goal setting, differentiated instruction and class observation, as well as work showcases and assessments— have significantly improved students' motivation, engagement, academic self-concept, self-efficacy, and academic performance. The core contribution of this study lies in providing a viable pathway to improve the academic performance of vocational college students by integrating Organizational Development (OD) into the classroom. By institutionalizing reflective practices (such as pre- and post-intervention analyses), higher education institutions can establish data-driven feedback loops to continuously align educational outcomes with market and societal demands

tittel: MENINGKATKAN KEMAMPUAN MENGGAMBAR KONSTRUKSI DENGAN MENGGUNAKAN SOFTWARE AUTOCAD: STUDI TENTANG EFEKTIVITAS MEDIA PEMBELAJARAN
sammendrag: Vocational high school students require several skills that will be utilized when they complete their studies in school. One of the desired skills is the ability to draw construction using the AutoCAD program. The ultimate skill expected from students is the capability to create construction drawings in the form of 2-D models. The primary focus of this research is to determine the extent to which AutoCAD can serve as an eflective learning tool in developing the construction drawing competence of vocational high school students. This study holds practical implications for teachers and educational institutions in vocational high schools by emphasizing the importance of integrating technology such as AutoCAD into the curriculum to prepare students with relevant and necessary skills for the construction industry. Consequently, the findings of this research can provide concrete guidance for the development of more eflective learning strategies at the vocational high school level.

tittel: From secondary STEM endorsement completion to postsecondary enrollment and STEM major choice
sammendrag: This study examined the association between STEM endorsement completion and postsecondary enrollment and STEM major choice among Texas public high school students. Using statewide longitudinal data from the Texas Education Research Center, we followed 106,788 students who entered 9th grade in 2014 and graduated in 2018. Guided by Social Cognitive Career Theory, binary logistic regression models assessed the role of STEM endorsement completion alongside sociodemographic characteristics and school academic context. Results indicated that STEM endorsement completion was strongly associated with both postsecondary enrollment and STEM major choice. Gender, race/ethnicity, socioeconomic status, immigrant status, career and technical education (CTE) participation, gifted/talented designation, and at-risk status were also significantly associated with postsecondary enrollment and STEM major choice. These findings highlight persistent equity gaps and underscore the importance of moving beyond pathway access toward equitable completion through targeted advising and structured secondary STEM supports.

tittel: International Models of Student Tracking into Vocational Pathways after Lower Secondary Education: Lessons for Vietnam
kilde: Dong Thap University Journal of Science
sammendrag: Student tracking into technical and vocational education and training (TVET) pathways following lower secondary education is increasingly recognized as a strategic approach to strengthening workforce development, facilitating school-to-work transitions, and driving sustainable economic growth. However, designing tracking systems that balance educational efficiency with social equity remains a significant policy challenge. Thus, this study identifies, compares, and evaluates major international models of TVET student tracking to derive transferable policy insights for Vietnam's post-Grade 9 education reforms. Using a qualitative comparative policy analysis approach, we synthesized peer-reviewed literature, international organization reports, and official policy documents. Findings reveal that successful tracking systems across diverse contexts consistently exhibit five core features: coherent governance, robust school–industry partnerships, comprehensive career guidance, flexible and permeable pathways, and tight alignment with labor market needs. Rather than replicating a single model, Vietnam should adapt these institutional principles to its specific socio-economic and cultural context. Ultimately, this study contributes to the comparative TVET literature and provides actionable, evidence-based recommendations to enhance governance, employer engagement, pathway flexibility, and lifelong learning in Vietnam.

tittel: A Causal-Comparative Study of Career Maturity in Young Adults and Early College Students in Career and Technical Education Programs
sammendrag: The purpose of this quantitative, causal-comparative study was to examine differences in career maturity between young adult and high school students enrolled in Career and Technical Education District programs at a rural community college in Arizona. Grounded in Social Learning Theory and Career Construction Theory, the study explored how early exposure to Career and Technical Education influences career maturity. The sample included 196 students, half high school Career and Technical Education District students and half young adults aged 18 to 24 participating in Career and Technical Education. Career maturity was measured using the Career Maturity Inventory Form C, which assessed concern, curiosity, confidence, and consultation. Surveys were administered online during class time with instructor coordination. A combination of analysis of variance and multivariate analysis of variance was used to assess group differences. This study filled a gap by linking Career and Technical Education dual enrollment to career maturity in rural contexts. Results indicated no statistically significant differences in overall career maturity or the career maturity subscales of concern, curiosity, confidence, and consultation between high school Career and Technical Education District students and young adult students enrolled in Career and Technical Education programs. The findings suggested that participation in dual enrollment Career and Technical Education pathways may support similar levels of career maturity among both adolescent and young adult students. Recommendations for future research included conducting longitudinal studies across multiple institutions and examining additional demographic variables influencing career maturity.

tittel: Dialoguing educational challenges: Understanding early school leaving and underachievement
sammendrag: This study investigates the perspectives of diverse stakeholders within schools and the broader educational landscape to identify gaps between prevention, intervention, and compensation measures, as outlined in the 2014 Eurydice report, and dimensions of student engagement conceptualised by Fredricks et al. (2004) (behavioural, cognitive, and emotional). Distinctively, the study engages multiple stakeholders, ranging from students to policymakers, in the co-construction of knowledge to address underachievement and early school leaving. Through a dialogic co-creation approach, it seeks to uncover discrepancies between policy intentions and educational practices that perpetuate barriers for learners from vulnerable backgrounds. This understanding aims to inform researchers, policymakers, and practitioners in developing more targeted and effective strategies for educational inclusion and equity. A qualitative methodology was employed, drawing on the dialogic seminar approach. This approach facilitates purposeful and egalitarian dialogue, recognising all participants, researchers and community members alike, as equally significant contributors to meaning-making. The participants (n = 35) included parents, students, teachers, school leaders and other school staff. Knowledge generation occurred through an intersubjective process that integrated the scientific expertise of researchers with the lived experiences and perspectives of participants. The participants identified significant gaps in existing policy measures and moved beyond critique to articulate grounded, actionable solutions, signalling a shift from fragmented reform initiatives toward a more participatory and contextually responsive model of educational policymaking. The findings highlight the need for a more integrated and relationally attuned policy framework, one that moves beyond fragmented interventions to promote system-wide coherence rooted in equity and student agency. Cultivating a policy culture that values sustained dialogic engagement among policymakers, practitioners, and learners is essential for ensuring that educational reform remains both socially just and contextually responsive.

tittel: Pathways, consequences, and community-proposed responses to school discontinuation in rural eastern Uganda: a qualitative study
sammendrag: BACKGROUND: Education is a social determinant of health, and incomplete schooling is associated with poorer sexual and reproductive health, psychosocial distress, and reduced economic opportunity. In Africa, many young people leave school before completing their educational cycle, yet qualitative evidence on the social and health consequences of discontinuation and on what affected communities view as appropriate responses remains limited. OBJECTIVE: To explore perspectives on the pathways, consequences, and proposed responses to school discontinuation in rural eastern Uganda. METHODS: = 15), purposively sampled with community assistance in Buyende and Kamuli districts in eastern Uganda. Data were analyzed using framework analysis. RESULTS: Three themes emerged. First, participants described discontinuation as driven by intersecting household poverty, school-level barriers, and gendered pressures including early marriage, teenage pregnancy, and sexual exploitation. Second, discontinuation was followed by psychological distress, social stigma, economic marginalization, and heightened vulnerability, particularly for young women. Third, participants proposed complementary supports spanning counseling and mentorship, vocational training and economic empowerment, and interpersonal and community-based engagement. CONCLUSIONS: School discontinuation in rural eastern Uganda is experienced as a cumulative process with cascading social, psychological, and economic consequences rather than a single educational event. Community members identified multi-domain responses addressing emotional recovery, livelihoods, and social reintegration together. These findings highlight the value of centering community perspectives when designing integrated interventions for young people affected by school discontinuation.

tittel: Culture, Literacy, and Academic Momentum in CTE Dual Enrollment Pathways
sammendrag: Career and technical education dual enrollment programs have expanded rapidly across the United States, driven by efforts to accelerate credential completion and expand workforce pathways for students historically underrepresented in higher education. Yet disparities in persistence and completion remain, disproportionately affecting students of color, low-income students, and first-generation college goers. One overlooked factor is the disciplinary literacy demands embedded in credentialed work, including field-specific communication norms and cultural assumptions built into pathway texts. Drawing on Wang (2017), Street (1984), Paris (2012), Ladson-Billings (1995), and Bailey et al. (2015), this analysis reframes literacy as both a driver and outcome of academic momentum. Mapping literacy across Wang's structural, academic, and psychosocial dimensions reveals how unscaffolded literacy demands create a cycle in which structural exclusion becomes academic strain, strain becomes psychosocial doubt, and doubt becomes the decision not to continue.

tittel: Competence Recognition, Workplace Culture, and Selective Absorption in a Triple Helix Fast-Track Pathway: A Qualitative Case Study from Indonesia
kilde: Journal of Culture and Values in Education
sammendrag: This study examines how the fast-track pathway in the two-year associate degree program (D2) linking a vocational high school, a polytechnic, and an industry partner operates as a cross-institutional arrangement for educational progression, competence recognition, workplace learning, and employment transition in Indonesia. A qualitative single-case study used semi-structured interviews, contextual non-participant observations, institutional and policy documents, and program artifacts, with data analyzed thematically. The findings reveal interconnected but institutionally distinct processes. Partnership governance operated through differentiated institutional roles, with the polytechnic acting as an intermediary between the vocational high school and the industry partner through recurring coordination and curriculum synchronization. The skill passport made prior competence visible across institutional boundaries, while Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) provided conditional, standards-based verification for academic progression. Extended industry immersion embedded workplace learning within the curriculum and supported professional socialization through authentic industrial participation. Selective absorption operated as an employer-side gatekeeping process during the transition to direct employment. Of 25 pathway participants documented in the program report, five were recruited by the industry partner, representing 20% direct absorption rather than the cohort's overall employment rate. Recruitment remained subject to selection requirements, workforce demand, and available positions. The case shows that competence recognition and workplace preparation can be institutionally coordinated while employment conversion remains governed by a distinct employer-side decision process. These findings highlight coordinated governance, credible competence recognition, sustained workplace learning, and transparent employment transition in vocational pathway design.

tittel: ZADOVOLJSTVO ŠKOLOM UČENIKA SA LAKOM INTELEKTUALNOM OMETENOŠĆU I UČENIKA TIPIČNOG RAZVOJA U SREDNJEM STRUČNOM OBRAZOVANJU
sammendrag: In the broader concept of life satisfaction, school satisfaction represents a specific domain related to students’ personal experience regarding how pleasant and fulfilled they find the school environment. The aim of this study is to examine differences in school satisfaction between students with mild intellectual disabilities and typically developing students, as well as to explore the impact of certain sociodemographic characteristics. The convenience sample consisted of 273 high school students enrolled in three-year vocational programs, divided into two groups. The first group included 138 students with developmental disabilities, while the second group comprised 135 typically developing students attending vocational high schools. Students' school satisfaction was assessed using a subscale of the Multidimensional Students' Life Satisfaction Scale. The obtained results unambiguously indicate that students with mild intellectual disabilities report significantly higher school satisfaction than their typically developing peers. This paper analyzes these differences with particular attention to the characteristics of the educational systems attended. Recommendations are provided for future research to further investigate school satisfaction, enabling a deeper understanding of students’ diverse needs stemming from their biopsychosocial characteristics. Based on these findings, educational stakeholders could more appropriately support the positive development of all students and implement targeted interventions aimed at improving the quality of school life.

tittel: Poverty Elimination Action Plan
sammendrag: This document fulfills the legislative requirements of LB 840, the Poverty Elimination Action Plan, aimed at reporting on Omaha efforts to eliminate poverty and developing a comprehensive strategy to eliminate poverty in Omaha, NE. It reviews research and policy interventions addressing poverty, incorporates community-driven and secondary data for a needs assessment, and offers actionable recommendations for poverty alleviation. The report also provides guidance on implementation, sustainability, and progress tracking. A brief conclusion at the end of this report is followed by appendices detailing supplementary data and analysis.

tittel: Pelatihan dan Pemagangan serta Peluang Kerja Pemuda di Indonesia: Analisis Data Sakernas 2022
sammendrag: Fluctuations in Indonesia’s economic growth have affected labor absorption amid an increasing labor force and a declining unemployment rate in 2022. Nevertheless, low labor competitiveness and skill mismatches with labor market demand remain major challenges, particularly for young people. This study aims to analyze the impact of training and apprenticeship on employment probability in Indonesia while accounting for potential selection bias in participation in skill-development programs. The study utilizes data from the August 2022 National Labor Force Survey (Sakernas), comprising 752,688 observations. The analytical method employed is Propensity Score Matching (PSM) to estimate the Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT), with employment status as the outcome variable and covariates including educational attainment, age, gender, area of residence, marital status, and school enrollment status. The estimation results indicate that participation in training has a positive and statistically significant effect on employment probability, increasing the likelihood of being employed by approximately 13–14 percentage points for training participants after matching. In addition, apprenticeship participation also exhibits a positive and significant impact on employment status, increasing employment probability by approximately 11 percentage points after controlling for observable individual characteristics. These findings suggest that both training and apprenticeship play an important role in improving employment opportunities, albeit through different mechanisms. Both indicate that skills development programmers can be an effective labour market policy instrument for improving youth transition to employment.

tittel: Akselerasi SDG 4 melalui Masterclass Beasiswa Pertamina Foundation di Universitas Islam Riau
sammendrag: Purpose: This Community Service (PKM) program aims to accelerate SDG 4 (Quality Education) by assisting Universitas Islam Riau students in preparing comprehensive scholarship application packages (essays and motivation letters) for the Pertamina Foundation scholarship. Method: The implementation method consists of four structured stages: preparation, intensive interactive mentoring, final evaluation, and achievement metrics data analysis. Results/findings: The intensive mentoring approach successfully improved participants' technical readiness. This is statistically indicated by a 9.99% increase in average pre-test to post-test scores (from 60.76% to 70.75%), backed by a 100% participant satisfaction rate on a Likert-scale survey. Conclusions: Through a responsive, two-way coaching approach, this program has demonstrably succeeded in enhancing the conceptual understanding, technical readiness, and learner autonomy of students at the Universitas Islam Riau in preparing scholarship application documents. Limitations: The scope of this study is constrained by technical network asymmetry, limited mentoring duration, and short-term evaluation metrics. Additionally, the study does not capture long-term sustainability effects, as post-intervention outcomes beyond the observation period were not assessed. Contributions: This program contributes to Academic Capacity Building and institutional SDG 4 acceleration by providing a highly effective, replicable intervention model for student financial attainment.

tittel: Opting for the shortcut: incidence, patterns, and economic benefits of shortened apprenticeship durations in Germany
kilde: Empirical research in vocational education and training
sammendrag: Abstract Despite its success in smoothing the transition from education to the labour market, the German system of apprenticeship training is often criticised as inflexible. Yet, under specific conditions, many apprentices can shorten the standard training duration by up to one year, either by agreeing a shorter duration when signing the contract or by obtaining early admission to the final examination. Empirically, little is known about how frequently these options are used and what economic consequences they have. Using the Vocational Training Statistics for 2008 to 2023, we show that, on average, 21% of newly signed apprenticeship contracts were shortened by at least six months, while 7.3% of the graduates of an apprenticeship used the option of preponed final exams. We then combine these descriptive results with simulations based on unique cost-benefit data on apprenticeship training. The simulations suggest sizeable monetary gains for both firms and apprentices: depending on the scenario, firms can reduce training costs by up to about EUR 9,000, whereas apprentices can gain up to about EUR 25,700 through earlier access to skilled-worker wages. These results indicate that institutionalised options to shorten training duration constitute an important and often overlooked source of flexibility in the German apprenticeship training system.

tittel: The long-run effects of public policy on human capital and savings
kilde: Oxford University Research Archive (ORA) (University of Oxford)
sammendrag: This thesis examines the long-run effects of a range of public policies on household decision- making, and their consequences for saving and human capital later in life. The first chapter looks at the effect of childcare subsidies on the decisions and outcomes of mothers, using a dynamic life-cycle model to estimate the labour supply and savings response to reduced child- care costs. This paper finds that a hypothetical universal childcare policy would significantly increased hours worked for mothers who were already in work, with a small but positive effect on earnings in the long run. The second chapter uses a similar model to estimate the savings response to changes to adult social care, examining how household consumption responds to changes to the level of insurance against social care costs individuals receive. The work outlines how greater social insurance would not trigger a larger saving response, but would be welfare-improving. The third chapter uses a difference-in-differences strategy to estimate the effect of a conditional cash transfer for young people staying in education on long-run outcomes, finding that the additional incentive to stay in school did not lead to increased wages later in life.

tittel: Koulutuksen merkitys rikoksista tuomittujen naisten elämänkulussa
sammendrag: This study focuses on the role of education at different stages of the life course of women convicted of crimes.The study examines how the life course and educational trajectories of these women were structured during childhood and adolescence, and how school environments supported their development into adulthood.In addition, the role of education in prison during adulthood is examined.The theoretical framework of this study is based on research traditions in life course and education, also including a criminological approach to the subject.The development into adulthood is examined within the framework of Positive Youth Development (PYD).Data were collected by interviewing 17 women convicts in different parts of Finland.The interview themes were life course progression through different age stages, its contextual dimensions, and the events of school paths.The data were analyzed using qualitative content analysis based on the concepts of life course research and PYD theory.Interviewees´ experiences of their life course and educational trajectories during childhood and adolescence divided them into four distinct groups.The findings indicated that the educational trajectories of the groups reflected the trajectories, transitions and turning points in the life course.6The support provided by school environments appeared to vary greatly from the perspective of development into adulthood of the interviewees.The educational setting supported their development in cognitive competence, but the support remained incomplete in other areas.Development into adulthood occurred favorably for those who received support in their school environments for the development of all five elements of PYD theory, namely connection, character, caring, competence and confidence.Correctional education served as a means of agency, enabling the interviewees to influence different dimensions of their life course within an environment characterized by restricted autonomy.The role of education in prison varied according to the life domains in which the functions of education were realized.The life course prior to and during the imprisonment of the interviewees, as well as their views of their future perspectives, were reflected in the role they assigned to education, including the development of confidence in their own capabilities.Overall, the educational trajectories became interwoven with the life course of the women studied, mirroring the events, transitions and turning points of different life stages.Experiences of school paths during childhood and adolescence -and the roles attributed to them -were reflected in adulthood as self efficacy and elements of well being, or as their absence.They became evident also in correctional education and in functions and roles assigned to it.The findings of this study can be applied in the design and implementation of pedagogical approaches and support measures in basic education, upper secondary level and correctional education.

tittel: BUILDING ORGANIZATIONAL COHERENCE IN RURAL CAREER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION: AN IMPROVEMENT SCIENCE EVALUATION OF LEADERSHIP STRUCTURE, STRUCTURED ADVISING, AND WORKFORCE ALIGNMENT
kilde: Scholar Works at UT Tyler (The University of Texas at Tyler)
sammendrag: Fewer than half of students enrolled in Career and Technical Education (CTE) courses in a rural Texas school district completed a full program of study, with disparities exceeding 20 percentage points among economically-disadvantaged students, emergent bilingual students, and students receiving special education services. This dissertation in practice examined these disparities as issues of system design rather than student readiness. The study was conducted in a district serving approximately 4,600 students, with a primary focus on its comprehensive high school of approximately 1,351 students. Using an improvement science framework and a convergent embedded mixed-methods design, the study examined three baseline years and one implementation year (2025–2026). Root cause analysis identified four primary barriers to CTE pathway completion: fragmented advising practices, the absence of a formal CTE leadership structure, misalignment between programs of study and regional workforce needs, and master scheduling practices that did not consistently support pathway completion. In response, the intervention included four coordinated components: a district CTE Leadership Team, a structured advising protocol, workforce-aligned program review, and Industry-Based Certification (IBC) monitoring. Each component was refined through iterative Plan–Do–Study–Act cycles. Analysis of archival district data demonstrated a statistically significant increase in IBC attainment (χ²(3, N = 5,311) = 250.73, p < .001, Cramér’s V = .22). IBC attainment increased from a pooled baseline rate of 4.4% to 17.5% during the implementation year, with 236 students earning at least one certification. Pathway completion rates remained relatively stable and were comparable across special education and economic status groups; however, emergent bilingual students experienced significantly lower completion rates. Certification gains were also uneven across student groups, with female, Hispanic/Latino, and at-risk students earning certifications at significantly lower rates than their peers. Thematic analysis of 17 interviews conducted with administrators, counselors, teachers, and industry partners identified five themes, including increased pathway awareness, stronger cross-role collaboration and shared accountability, and greater program relevance. Because the study did not include a control group, the findings should be interpreted as associational rather than causal. The findings suggested that equitable CTE improvement requires organizational coherence through intentional leadership structures, clearly assigned advising responsibilities, workforce-aligned programming, and ongoing disaggregated outcome monitoring. The results further demonstrate that improvement in one CTE outcome does not necessarily translate into equitable improvement across all outcomes or student groups. Keywords: career and technical education, rural schools, improvement science, PDSA, equity, industry-based certification, workforce alignment

tittel: From Vocational Training to Formal Employment: Evaluating the Impact of Government-Funded Scholarships on Vulnerable Youth
sammendrag: Purpose: This study evaluated the effectiveness of Life Skills Education (Pendidikan Kecakapan Kerja/PKK) and Entrepreneurship Education (Pendidikan Kecakapan Wirausaha/PKW) scholarship programs in enhancing human resource competencies and reducing unemployment and poverty.Methodology: Using the ADDIE model (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation), data were collected from scholarship recipients, training institutions, education authorities, employer associations, and industry representatives in Bekasi City, Bekasi Regency, and Karawang Regency in West Java.Results: The findings show that program planning and development comprehensively involved stakeholders. However, evaluation outcomes indicate limited sustainability, with employment absorption among PKK participants reaching 69.7%, and approximately 70% of PKW participants pursuing self-employment.Conclusions: The programs have contributed to improving skills but have not fully achieved sustainable economic empowerment for women. Training aligned with industry needs is essential to strengthen employment opportunities and economic mobility.Limitations: This study covered only three districts in West Java, limiting the generalizability of the findings for national implementation.Contributions: This study advances vocational education research by demonstrating how outcome-based evaluation, curriculum responsiveness, and industry engagement jointly strengthen the effectiveness of scholarship-based vocational training programs.

tittel: Effects of an Integrated Intervention for Improving Student Academic Engagement and Disruptive Behavior in High School
sammendrag: The transition to high school can be a difficult time for students with disabilities given increased academic expectations, larger school sizes, and greater student autonomy. Moreover, students struggling to stay academically engaged in core content classes are at greater risk for poor academic outcomes and school failure. This experimental pilot study examined the preliminary effects of an integrated Tier 2 intervention designed to improve academic engagement and reduce disruptive behaviors. To evaluate the intervention, we conducted an experimental single-case concurrent multiple-baseline design across four students. Three ninth-grade students were either receiving special education services or a 504 plan. The intervention included teaching students academic and behavioral engagement skills, followed by brief, ongoing coaching sessions on these skills every other day. Results indicated that the intervention had a moderate effect on student academic engagement, and both teachers and students rated the intervention as socially acceptable. Due to the lack of disruptive behaviors observed across the students, we were unable to evaluate the effects of the intervention on disruptive behaviors. Implications for research and practice surrounding the transition of ninth-grade students with or at risk for disabilities are discussed.

tittel: Exploring the Integration of Emerging Technologies in Skills-Based TVET Curricula in Secondary Schools: A Critical Review
kilde: Asian Journal of Education and Social Studies
sammendrag: Technical and vocational education and training at secondary level is under sustained pressure to incorporate artificial intelligence, immersive simulation, automation, robotics and related digital technologies into curricula organised around occupational skills. Policy discourse often treats such integration as self-evidently beneficial, yet the empirical basis for this assumption has not been critically consolidated for the secondary phase, where learners are younger, provision is largely school-based and resource constraints are acute. This critical narrative review examines how emerging technologies are being integrated into skills-based secondary vocational curricula, what the evidence shows about their effects on learning and transition outcomes, and which conditions shape implementation. Peer-reviewed studies and institutional reports published from 2011 onwards were identified through education-specific and multidisciplinary scholarly indexes, citation tracking and searches of intergovernmental sources, and were appraised for design adequacy, contextual relevance and outcome validity. The synthesis indicates that curricula are changing more slowly and more unevenly than forecasts of automation imply, and that curriculum documents tend to emphasise tool use over broader digital and occupational competence. Immersive and simulation-based technologies show the most consistent short-term benefits for cognitive and procedural outcomes, although these benefits shrink or disappear when comparison conditions are equally well designed, and greater realism or presence does not reliably translate into better learning. Evidence on learning factories, artificial intelligence and generative tools in secondary vocational settings remains largely descriptive, perception-based or developmental. Teacher digital competence, institutional support, infrastructure and links with workplaces appear to shape integration more strongly than the technologies themselves, while patterns by gender, disability, location and income suggest that technology-rich provision can reproduce rather than reduce inequality. Major unresolved questions concern transfer to authentic work, long-term labour-market returns, the balance between general and occupation-specific skills, and the governance of data-driven tools. The review proposes an integrative framework that separates supported from hypothesised relationships and argues that integration should be judged by its contribution to durable vocational competence rather than by technological novelty.

tittel: Long-run impacts of school-based mentoring for at-risk youth: evidence from a randomized field experiment
sammendrag: This paper examines the long-term impact of a randomized experiment offering intensive mentoring to adolescent students. In the short term, the program reduced school dropout by 40%. By linking the experimental data to administrative records, the impact can be assessed up to 13 years after the start of the program. We find that, in the long run, the program increased schooling while reducing suspicion of crime and decreasing family size. The positive schooling effects are concentrated among high-risk students, who also appear to earn higher wages. On the other hand, the program has no clear impact on the outcomes of low-risk students.

tittel: UPAYA GURU BIMBINGAN DAN KONSELING DALAM MENGATASI KENAKALAN REMAJA PADA SISWA KELAS XI: STUDI LITERATUR di SMA NEGERI 3 KUPANG
kilde: Jurnal pendidikan Indonesia Teori Penelitian dan Inovasi
sammendrag: Adolescent delinquency at the senior high school level remains a persistent issue requiring a professional response through Guidance and Counseling services. This study aims to analyze the efforts of guidance counselors in addressing juvenile delinquency through preventive, corrective, and collaborative service approaches. The research employs a qualitative method with a literature review, examining scholarly articles, books, educational regulations, and professional publications related to counseling interventions for problematic student behavior. The findings indicate that the effectiveness of counselor interventions is influenced by the quality of basic services, individual counseling, cooperation with homeroom teachers and parents, and the school’s ability to build a supportive educational climate. Scientifically, this article contributes by presenting a comprehensive synthesis of recent research findings regarding the role of guidance and counseling teachers in addressing juvenile delinquency. This can serve as a conceptual and practical foundation for developing guidance and counseling service programs at the high school level.ABSTRAK Kenakalan remaja di tingkat sekolah menengah atas tetap menjadi masalah yang persisten dan memerlukan tanggapan profesional melalui layanan Bimbingan dan Konseling. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis upaya konselor bimbingan dalam menangani kenakalan remaja melalui pendekatan layanan preventif, korektif, dan kolaboratif. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kualitatif dengan tinjauan literatur, menganalisis artikel ilmiah, buku, peraturan pendidikan, dan publikasi profesional yang berkaitan dengan intervensi konseling untuk perilaku siswa yang bermasalah. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa efektivitas intervensi konselor dipengaruhi oleh kualitas layanan dasar, konseling individu, kerja sama dengan guru kelas dan orang tua, serta kemampuan sekolah dalam membangun iklim pendidikan yang mendukung. Secara ilmiah, artikel ini berkontribusi dengan menyajikan sintesis komprehensif dari temuan penelitian terbaru mengenai peran guru bimbingan dan konseling dalam menangani kenakalan remaja. Hal ini dapat menjadi landasan konseptual dan praktis untuk mengembangkan program layanan bimbingan dan konseling di tingkat sekolah menengah atas.

tittel: School Connectedness: Using School Websites to Foster a Sense of Belonging in School
kilde: RIT Scholar Works (Rochester Institute of Technology)
sammendrag: The current study explored the relationships between adolescents' internet use, feelings of school connectedness, social anxiety, and interest in the school's website. Participants were 8th (n = 121) and 11th (n = 71) grade students from a rural upstate New York, middle and high school. Data was collected using the Social Use of the Internet Survey, which was designed to measure participants' internet use, interest in the school's website, feelings of school connectedness and loneliness. No significant mean differences were present between the 8th and 11th grade groups on school connectedness and on interest in the school's website. Multiple regression analysis showed that for both 8th and 11th grade samples, loneliness was a significant negative predictor of school connectedness. School connectedness and school contact via e-mail were significant predictors of school website interest among the 8 n grade sample, while in the 1 1th grade sample, being bullied was a significant predicator of school website interest. The qualitative findings of this study provide the school with valuable information regarding students' interest in using their school website, participants' preferred online activities and opinions of their school website.

tittel: Creating Effective Mentoring Relationships with Urban Youth
kilde: SUNY Digital Repository Support (State University of New York System)
sammendrag: This project is an initial investigation into student perceptions of the “Family of Five” mentoring program in this school The Family of Five program in this school is designed to reengage disenfranchised youth in the educational system. All staff members at this school are asked to mentor a family of five students. Staff members are asked to meet with each of the five students on a weekly basis, monitor their academic progress, develop a relationship with the students family and provide an opportunity for the student to develop a supportive relationship with adults in this school. Many of this school’s students have a significant history of poor academic performance, disciplinary issues, and truancy. This project will explore the students’ perceptions of their educational experience as part of the Family of Five program. The information gathered from this project will be used to develop future programming to support the students at this school. This project is conducted under the premises that students who feel supported by the adults in their lives will increase their ability to be academically successful.

tittel: Parent Attendance at Teacher Conferences: A Comparison of Students with Risk Factors of Dropout
sammendrag: Denfeld High School in Duluth, Minnesota between the rate of "dropout risk factors " of students whose parents signed up to attend teacher conferences in September of 2009 and students in the total school population. Another goal is to find out if there is a difference between the rate of "dropout risk factors " of students at Denfeld whose parents did not sign up to attend teacher conferences and the students with risk factors whose parents signed up to attend teacher conferences. A final purpose was to determine out of all the students at Denfeld High School in the first grade period in the fall of 2009 with "dropout risk factors " what percent are students of parent(s) who signed up to attend teacher conferences in fall 2009. The risk factors considered in this study are: 1. Low socioeconomic status (students who qualify for free or reduced lunch), 2. low academic achievement (students who received at least one grade of "P ' in the first grade period of the 2009-2010 school year), 3. poor behavior (students who received at least one behavior referral in the first grade period during fall of 2009) and 4. truancy (students who missed at least 18 classes unrelated to school activities in the first grade period). Methods This study examines risk factor trends in all the 973 students enrolled at Denf eld and the 300 students whose parents signed up to attend teacher conferences in September of 2009. This research study is descriptive in nature and uses secondary data to determine whether there was a difference in risk factors of dropout in the general student population at Denfeld compared to the students whose parents signed up to attend teacher conferences. The secondary data was compiled from the Denfeld student data base (infinite campus) to determine which risk factors Denfeld students had. Percentages of the Denfeld student population with risk factors were compared to the percentages of the student population whose parents signed up to attend teacher conferences.

tittel: The effectiveness of a career course on program of study selection and career maturity of high school freshmen
sammendrag: Supporting career development in adolescents is a perplexing issue for educators. In response, educators are implementing various interventions assisting students in the exploration process. The purpose of this causal comparative study was to determine the effect of the career education course employed by a rural high school in Tennessee on student selection of a program of study and career maturity. Upon completion of the semester, a convenient sample of 79 ninth grade students completed the Career Maturity Inventory-form C along with a program of study selection inquiry. Data analysis did not determine a statistical difference in high school career maturity and selection of a program of study based on completion of a career exploration course. A chi square test of independence was conducted to analyze the association between the 2 categorical variables of a career management success course and selection of a program-of-study. A one-way multivariate analysis of variance (MANOVA) was conducted to analyze the effect of the career course on the linear combination of the subscale scores of the career maturity inventory. Analysis did not provide evidence to reject the 7 null hypotheses. The study did illustrate that students at Nosre Academy were on average gaining the knowledge to select a program of study and had on average developed career maturity at a higher average than norms established for the instrument. Recommendations for further research include additional constructs being considered along with further examination of the impact of the Appalachian culture.

tittel: Disengagement from and reintegration to school : a narrative enquiry
sammendrag: This study utilized a narrative inquiry design to examine the process of disengagement from and reintegration to school among five former at-risk students, with an emphasis on participants' perspectives on and interpretations of this process.In-depth, unstructured interviews provided the data for the resulting narrative accounts.Five individual narratives of disengagement and reintegration were produced.A cross case thematic 1 temporal analysis of these narratives suggested the existence of three movements which characterized the process of disengagement and reintegration to school: Early problems and the search for belonging; The middle years and the struggle to survive; and From atrisk to risk taker: agency, relationships and the road to graduation.Disengagement and reintegration, for these participants, resembled a roller coaster ride.Participants reported a growing disenchantment with various aspects of their early life and an escalating series of problems across numerous domains.This was followed by a middle period characterized by a series of disengaging experiences and continued attempts to reengage.A critical period defined by an increasing intensity of both personal difficulties and indepth self examination served as the catalyst for the final movement during which participants reintegrated to school and achieved secondary school graduation.A framework for understanding reintegration based on the development of agency and the primacy of caring relationships is presented in conjunction with implications for education and educational leadership.iii Dedication For Kiera.May the wonder and joy of learning be forever yours.

tittel: Perceptions of school climate and connectedness: The impact of a cross age peer mentoring program
A Little Now for a Lot Later: A Look at a Texas Advanced Placement Incentive Program
sammendrag: I analyze a program implemented in Texas schools serving underprivileged populations that pays both students and teachers for passing grades on Advanced Placement (AP) examinations. Using a difference-in-differences strategy, I find that program adoption is associated with increased AP course and exam taking, increases in the number of students with high SAT/ACT scores, and increases in college matriculation. The rewards don't appear to distort behaviors in undesirable ways, and I present evidence that teachers and students were not simply maximizing rewards. Guidance counselors credit the improvements to greater AP access, changes in social norms towards APs, and better student information.

tittel: Agents of Change: Pathways through Which Mentoring Relationships Influence Adolescents' Academic Adjustment
sammendrag: A conceptual model was tested in which the effects of mentoring relationships on adolescents' academic outcomes were hypothesized to be mediated partially through improvements in parental relationships. The parameters of the model were compared with those of an alternative, in which improved parental relationships were treated as an outcome variable rather than a mediator. The study included 959 young adolescents (M age = 12.25 years), all of whom applied to Big Brothers Big Sisters programs. The adolescents were randomly assigned to either the treatment or control group and administered questions at baseline and 18 months later. The hypothesized model provided a significantly better explanation of the data than the alternative. In addition to improvements in parental relationships, mentoring led to reductions in unexcused absences and improvements in perceived scholastic competence. Direct effects of mentoring on global self-worth, school value, and grades were not detected but were instead mediated through improved parental relationships and scholastic competence. Implications of the findings for theory and research are discussed.

tittel: Remedying Education: Evidence from Two Randomized Experiments in India
sammendrag: This paper presents the results of two randomized experiments conducted in schools in urban India. A remedial education program hired young women to teach students lagging behind in basic literacy and numeracy skills. It increased average test scores of all children in treatment schools by 0.28 standard deviation, mostly due to large gains experienced by children at the bottom of the test-score distribution. A computer-assisted learning program focusing on math increased math scores by 0.47 standard deviation. One year after the programs were over, initial gains remained significant for targeted children, but they faded to about 0.10 standard deviation.

tittel: Manipulation Testing Based on Density Discontinuity
kilde: The Stata Journal Promoting communications on statistics and Stata
sammendrag: In this article, we introduce two community-contributed commands, rddensity and rdbwdensity, that implement automatic manipulation tests based on density discontinuity and are constructed using the results for local-polynomial density estimators in Cattaneo, Jansson, and Ma (2017b, Simple local polynomial density estimators, Working paper, University of Michigan). These new tests exhibit better size properties (and more power under additional assumptions) than other conventional approaches currently available in the literature. The first command, rddensity, implements manipulation tests based on a novel local-polynomial density estimation technique that avoids prebinning of the data (improving size properties) and allows for restrictions on other features of the model (improving power properties). The second command, rdbwdensity, implements several bandwidth selectors specifically tailored for the manipulation tests discussed herein. We also provide a companion R package with the same syntax and capabilities as rddensity and rdbwdensity.

tittel: Financial Incentives and Student Achievement: Evidence from Randomized Trials
sammendrag: This paper describes a series of school-based randomized trials in over 250 urban schools designed to test the impact of financial incentives on student achievement.In stark contrast to simple economic models, our results suggest that student incentives increase achievement when the rewards are given for inputs to the educational production function, but incentives tied to output are not effective.Relative to popular education reforms of the past few decades, student incentives based on inputs produce similar gains in achievement at lower costs.Qualitative data suggest that incentives for inputs may be more effective because students do not know the educational production function, and thus have little clue how to turn their excitement about rewards into achievement.Several other models, including lack of self-control, complementary inputs in production, or the unpredictability of outputs, are also consistent with the experimental data.

tittel: Conditional Cash Transfers and Their Impact on Child Work and Schooling: Evidence from the PROGRESA Program in Mexico
sammendrag: Evidence from the PROGRESA Program in Mexico O ver the past few years, a number of Latin American countries have introduced antipoverty programs specifically focused toward increasing investment in human capital, as measured, in particular, by education, but also by health and nutrition.These programs represent a significant departure from previous antipoverty policies within the region, for they are based on the premise that one of the fundamental causes of poverty and its intergenerational transmission is the lack of investment in human development.A distinguishing characteristic of the programs is the provision of cash transfers on the condition that poor families take their children out of work and send them to school.One of the first programs of this kind to be implemented was Mexico's Programa de Educación, Salud y Alimentación (the Education, Health, and Nutrition Program), known by its Spanish acronym, PROGRESA.Introduced in 1997, the program, which provides cash transfers, is aimed at increasing families' investment in human capital as defined by education, health, and nutrition.To achieve this objective, PROGRESA conditions cash transfers on children's enrollment and regular attendance in school, as well as clinic attendance.These transfers correspond, on average, to a 22 percent increase in the income levels of the beneficiary families and are given directly to the mother of the family.The program also includes inkind health benefits and nutritional supplements for children up to age five 45

tittel: Latin America's Social Policy Challenge: Education, Social Insurance, Redistribution
sammendrag: Long regarded as a region beset by macroeconomic instability, high inflation, and excessive poverty and inequality, Latin America has undergone a major transformation over the last 20 years. The region has seen improved macroeconomic management and substantial and sustained reductions in poverty and inequality. In this paper, we argue that social policy, including human capital and education, social insurance, and redistribution, need special attention if achievements of the last two decades are to be sustained and amplified. Starting in the mid 1990s, many governments in the region introduced a variety of programs, including noncontributory pensions and health insurance, and cash transfers targeted to the poor. Social spending in Latin America increased sharply. These policies have been widely praised, and we believe they have resulted in substantial improvements in the lives of the poor in the region. However, a more nuanced view shows some worrisome trends. Moving forward, we believe it is necessary to pay much closer attention to the quality of services, particularly in education; to the incentives generated by the interplay of some programs, particularly in the labor market; to a more balanced intertemporal distribution of benefits, particularly between young and old; and to sustainable sources of finance, particularly to the link between contributions and benefits.

tittel: Measuring the Impacts of Teachers II: Teacher Value-Added and Student Outcomes in Adulthood
sammendrag: Are teachers' impacts on students' test scores (value-added) a good measure of their quality? This question has sparked debate partly because of a lack of evidence on whether high value-added (VA) teachers improve students' long-term outcomes. Using school district and tax records for more than one million children, we find that students assigned to high-VA teachers are more likely to attend college, earn higher salaries, and are less likely to have children as teenagers. Replacing a teacher whose VA is in the bottom 5 percent with an average teacher would increase the present value of students' lifetime income by approximately $250,000 per classroom. (JEL H75, I21, J24, J45)

tittel: Experimental Estimates of Education Production Functions
sammendrag: This paper analyzes data on 11,600 students and their teachers who were randomly assigned to different size classes from kindergarten through third grade. Statistical methods are used to adjust for nonrandom attrition and transitions between classes. The main conclusions are (1) on average, performance on standardized tests increases by four percentile points the first year students attend small classes; (2) the test score advantage of students in small classes expands by about one percentile point per year in subsequent years; (3) teacher aides and measured teacher characteristics have little effect; (4) class size has a larger effect for minority students and those on free lunch; (5) Hawthorne effects were unlikely.

tittel: Human Capital Policy
Making a Difference. An Impact Study of Big Brothers/Big Sisters.
The Benefit of Additional High-School Math and Science Classes for Young Men and Women
kilde: Journal of Business and Economic Statistics
sammendrag: Phillip B. Levine, David J. Zimmerman, The Benefit of Additional High-School Math and Science Classes for Young Men and Women, Journal of Business & Economic Statistics, Vol. 13, No. 2, JBES Symposium on Program and Policy Evaluation (Apr., 1995), pp. 137-149

tittel: Addressing Non-Financial Barriers to College Access and Success: Evidence and Policy Implications
sammendrag: Non-financial barriers to college are an important possible explanation for socioeconomic, racial, gender, and other gaps in college access and success.A sizeable economic literature documents policy efforts to understand and address these barriers.We review this literature on non-financial interventions for improving college access and success ranging from discreet and narrowly defined interventions to comprehensive and multifaceted programs and systemic-level solutions.

tittel: Education, Income and Mobility: Experimental Impacts of Childhood Exposure to Progresa after 20 Years
sammendrag: In 1997, the Mexican government designed the conditional cash transfer program Progresa, which became the worldwide model of a new approach to social programs, simultaneously targeting human capital accumulation and poverty reduction. A large literature has documented the short and medium-term impacts of the Mexican program and its successors in other countries. Using Progresas experimental evaluation design originally rolled out in 1997-2000, and a tracking survey conducted 20 years later, this paper studies the differential long-term impacts of exposure to Progresa. We focus on two cohorts of children: i) those that during the period of differential exposure were in-utero or in the first years of life, and ii) those who during the period of differential exposure were transitioning from primary to secondary school. Results for the early childhood cohort, 18-20-year-old at endline, shows that differential exposure to Progresa during the early years led to positive impacts on educational attainment and labor income expectations. This constitutes unique long-term evidence on the returns of an at-scale intervention on investments in human capital during the first 1000 days of life. Results for the school cohort - in their early 30s at endline - show that the short-term impacts of differential exposure to Progresa on schooling were sustained in the long-run and manifested themselves in larger labor incomes, more geographical mobility including through international migration, and later family formation.

tittel: Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data
sammendrag: The second edition of this acclaimed graduate text provides a unified treatment of two methods used in contemporary econometric research, cross section and data panel methods. By focusing on assumptions that can be given behavioral content, the book maintains an appropriate level of rigor while emphasizing intuitive thinking. The analysis covers both linear and nonlinear models, including models with dynamics and/or individual heterogeneity. In addition to general estimation frameworks (particular methods of moments and maximum likelihood), specific linear and nonlinear methods are covered in detail, including probit and logit models and their multivariate, Tobit models, models for count data, censored and missing data schemes, causal (or treatment) effects, and duration analysis. Econometric Analysis of Cross Section and Panel Data was the first graduate econometrics text to focus on microeconomic data structures, allowing assumptions to be separated into population and sampling assumptions. This second edition has been substantially updated and revised. Improvements include a broader class of models for missing data problems; more detailed treatment of cluster problems, an important topic for empirical researchers; expanded discussion of generalized instrumental variables (GIV) estimation; new coverage (based on the author's own recent research) of inverse probability weighting; a more complete framework for estimating treatment effects with panel data, and a firmly established link between econometric approaches to nonlinear panel data and the generalized estimating equation literature popular in statistics and other fields. New attention is given to explaining when particular econometric methods can be applied; the goal is not only to tell readers what does work, but why certain obvious procedures do not. The numerous included exercises, both theoretical and computer-based, allow the reader to extend methods covered in the text and discover new insights.

tittel: A meta-analytic review of experiments examining the effects of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation.
sammendrag: A meta-analysis of 128 studies examined the effects of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation. As predicted, engagement-contingent, completion-contingent, and performance-contingent rewards significantly undermined free-choice intrinsic motivation (d = -0.40, -0.36, and -0.28, respectively), as did all rewards, all tangible rewards, and all expected rewards. Engagement-contingent and completion-contingent rewards also significantly undermined self-reported interest (d = -0.15, and -0.17), as did all tangible rewards and all expected rewards. Positive feedback enhanced both free-choice behavior (d = 0.33) and self-reported interest (d = 0.31). Tangible rewards tended to be more detrimental for children than college students, and verbal rewards tended to be less enhancing for children than college students. The authors review 4 previous meta-analyses of this literature and detail how this study's methods, analyses, and results differed from the previous ones.

tittel: Intrinsic and Extrinsic Motivation
sammendrag: A central tenet of economics is that individuals respond to incentives. For psychologists and sociologists, in contrast, rewards and punishments are often counterproductive, because they undermine “intrinsic motivation”. We reconcile these two views, showing how performance incentives offered by an informed principal (manager, teacher, parent) can adversely impact an agent's (worker, child) perception of the task, or of his own abilities. Incentives are then only weak reinforcers in the short run, and negative reinforcers in the long run. We also study the effects of empowerment, help and excuses on motivation, as well as situations of ego bashing reflecting a battle for dominance within a relationship.

tittel: The Importance of Noncognitive Skills: Lessons from the GED Testing Program
sammendrag: The Importance of Noncognitive Skills: Lessons from the GED Testing Program by James J. Heckman and Yona Rubinstein. Published in volume 91, issue 2, pages 145-149 of American Economic Review, May 2001

tittel: Into College, Out of Poverty? Policies to Increase the Postsecondary Attainment of the Poor
sammendrag: We review the experimental and quasi-experimental research evidence on the causal relationship between college costs and educational attainment, with a particular focus on low-income populations. The weight of the evidence indicates that reducing college costs can increase college entry and persistence. Simple and transparent programs appear to be most effective. Programs that link money to incentives and/or the takeup of academic support services appear to be particularly effective.

tittel: Making a Difference in Schools: The Big Brothers Big Sisters School-Based Mentoring Impact Study.
Conditional Cash Transfers: The Case of Progresa/Oportunidades
sammendrag: Conditional cash transfer (CCT) programs innovate by conditioning transfers to poor families on investments in the human capital of children and other family members. The Mexican CCT program Progresa/Oportunidades began in 1997 and has served as a model for many of the now over sixty countries with CCTs around the world, in large part due to its initial evaluation with an experimental design and numerous follow-up studies. This article reviews the literature on the development, evaluation, and findings of Progresa/Oportunidades, summarizing what is known about program effects, taking into account corrections for multiple-hypothesis testing. ( JEL H23, I18, I28, I32, I38, O15)

tittel: Targeted Remedial Education for Under-Performing Teenagers: Costs and Benefits
sammendrag: There is renewed interest in ways to enhance secondary education, especially among disadvantaged students.This study evaluates the short-term effects of a remedial-education program that provided additional instruction to under-performing high-school students in Israel.The program targeted 10th ntwelfth graders who needed additional help to pass the matriculation exams.Using a comparison group of schools that enrolled in the program later and implementing a differences-in-differences estimation strategy, we found that the program raised the school mean matriculation rate by 3.3 percentage points.This gain reflects mainly an effect on targeted participants and the absence of externalities on their untreated peers.The program was found to be less cost-effective than two alternative interventions based on incentives for teachers and students.

tittel: School Dropouts and Conditional Cash Transfers: Evidence from a Randomised Controlled Trial in Rural China's Junior High Schools
sammendrag: The overall goal of this study is to examine if there is a dropout problem in rural China and to explore the effectiveness of a Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) programme on the rate of dropping out. To meet this goal, we conduct a randomised controlled trial (RCT) to assess the impact of the CCT using a sample of the poorest 300 junior high school students in a nationally-designated poor county in Northwest China. We find that the annual dropout rate in the study county was 7.8 per cent and even higher, 13.3 per cent, among the children of poor households. We demonstrate that a CCT program reduces dropout by 60 per cent. The programme is most effective among students with poor academic performance, and likely more effective among girls and younger students.

tittel: Mentoring and Young People A literature review
kilde: OpenGrey (Institut de l'Information Scientifique et Technique)
sammendrag: This literature review was undertaken in response to the Beattie report, ‘Implementing inclusiveness: realising potential’. The report was commissioned by The Advisory Committee on Post-School Education and Training of Young People with Special Needs in April 1998 and examines the range of needs among young people who require additional support to participate in post-school education or training in Scotland. This client group is defined as young people aged 16-24 years and most at risk of social exclusion due to a range of factors such as physical disabilities, mental health problems, learning difficulties or disabilities, low educational attainment, and homelessness. The literature review explores the use of mentors in supporting these young people in their transition to post-school education, training, and employment. It covers published literature from the UK and the US from 1995 onwards. Some other literature in the form of conference papers and internet sources has been included where relevant. The review is not comprehensive but concentrates on the core area of mentoring with young people, occasionally drawing on work in related areas when appropriate. Key questions addressed by the review are: What is a mentor/mentoring? What is the evidence of positive outcomes for young people? What works? What doesn’t work? Is there a case for regulation? What are the views of mentees? What are the view of mentors? What are the views of commissioning bodies and/or employers? As part of the specification of the review, work by Carol Fitzgibbon of Durham University that examines the impact of identifying ‘underaspiring’ pupils is included in Appendix A. Appendix B outlines the search strategies used to identify the literature.

tittel: The Production of Human Capital in Developed Countries: Evidence from 196 Randomized Field Experiments
sammendrag: Randomized field experiments designed to better understand the production of human capital have increased exponentially over the past several decades.This chapter summarizes what we have learned about various partial derivatives of the human capital production function, what important partial derivatives are left to be estimated, and what -together -our collective efforts have taught us about how to produce human capital in developed countries.The chapter concludes with a back of the envelope simulation of how much of the racial wage gap in America might be accounted for if human capital policy focused on best practices gleaned from randomized field experiments.

tittel: The Impact of Chicago's Small High School Initiative
Two-Way Fixed Effects Estimators with Heterogeneous Treatment Effects
sammendrag: Linear regressions with period and group fixed effects are widely used to estimate treatment effects. We show that they estimate weighted sums of the average treatment effects (ATE ) in each group and period, with weights that may be negative. Due to the negative weights, the linear regression coefficient may for instance be negative while all the ATEs are positive. We propose another estimator that solves this issue. In the two applications we revisit, it is significantly different from the linear regression estimator. (JEL C21, C23, D72, J31, J51, L82)

kilde: Revue de l Institut International de Statistique / Review of the International Statistical Institute

tittel: Education for Growth: Why and for Whom?
sammendrag: This paper summarizes and tries to reconcile evidence from the microeconometric and empirical macro growth literatures on the effect of schooling on income and GDP growth. Much microeconometric evidence suggests that education is an important causal determinant of income for individuals within countries. At a national level, however, recent studies have found that increases in educational attainment are unrelated to economic growth. This discrepancy appears to be a result of the high rate of measurement error in first-differenced cross-country education data. After accounting for measurement error, the effect of changes in educational attainment on income growth in cross-country data is at least as great as microeconometric estimates of the rate of return to years of schooling. Another finding of the macro growth literature—that economic growth depends positively on the initial stock of human capital—is not robust when the assumption of a constant-coefficient model is relaxed.
