Results: = 204) of the parents were comfortable with connecting their child with an adult mentor online. Parents who reported being comfortable were more likely to be male, be White/Caucasian, have higher levels of education, be experienced with various social media platforms, be concerned about their child's aggression, have children with poorer behavioral health, and believe their children were using substances. Conclusion: Understanding the types of parents who are and are not comfortable with online mentoring, particularly for issues such as substance use prevention, may allow for better targeting and tailoring of recruitment efforts for online youth mentoring programs addressing sensitive health issues.

tittel: Connecting families through cash transfers and an enabling environment in Colombia, Mexico, and the Philippines: a qualitative study
sammendrag: Nearly 700 million people worldwide live in extreme poverty, and almost half of the world’s population lives below the poverty line. Cash transfer programs are increasingly used to address poverty’s effects on family well-being, yet less is known about how families experience programs that combine cash transfers with peer-driven mutual aid. Children International’s (CI) Community Independence Initiative (CII) provides conditional cash transfers and promotes family-led goal setting, mutual support, and shared learning. This qualitative study explored how families in Colombia, Mexico, and the Philippines experienced CII and made meaning of its material and relational components. We conducted focus groups with 51 adult and child participants from families who had completed CII. Thematic analysis revealed three themes that together reflected participants’ experience of CII over time: (1) Entering CII amid persistent family and economic strain; (2) Experiencing CII as both material support and collective problem-solving; and (3) Carrying forward connection and resilience while economic hardship persisted. Participants described CII as meaningful not only because of the cash transfers, which helped families meet immediate needs and invest in priorities such as education, household needs, health, and small businesses, but also because of the peer-driven structure that supported shared learning, mutual aid, family communication, and social connection. Although some relational and resilience-related benefits endured after the program ended, families continued to experience substantial economic hardship. Findings suggest that anti-poverty initiatives may be strengthened by integrating flexible material support with opportunities for peer connection and collective problem-solving, while also recognizing the limits of time-limited interventions in the context of persistent structural poverty.

tittel: Ekte arbeidsoppgaver kontra rom for å feile: et lærerperspektiv på hvordan læring i skole og læring i praksis forbereder yrkesfagelever på arbeidslivet
sammendrag: Å utdanne fremtidige yrkesutøvere er et sentralt mål i yrkesfaglige utdanningsprogram. I Norge følger yrkesfaglig opplæring normalt 2+2-modellen: to år i videregående skole etterfulgt av læretid i bedrift. I de to første årene kombinerer elevene opplæring på skolen med noe praksis i arbeidslivet gjennom faget yrkesfaglig fordypning (YFF). I denne artikkelen undersøker vi fra et lærerperspektiv hvordan læring i skolen og i praksis i arbeidslivet forbereder elever til arbeidslivet og læretiden. Datagrunnlaget er intervjuer med yrkesfaglærere fra tre programområder på andre året i videregående skole. I analysen tar vi utgangspunkt i teoretiske perspektiver på læringsmiljø og læring på ulike arenaer. Funnene synliggjør hva som kjennetegner de to læringsarenaene: Skolen tilbyr en trygg læringsarena hvor elevene kan prøve og feile, lære teoretiske begreper og øve systematisk på arbeidsoppgaver, samtidig som de beholder tilhørigheten til et ungdomsmiljø. I praksis i arbeidslivet vektlegges reelle oppgaver, normer, tempo og ansvar, som særlig utvikler relasjonell og situasjonsavhengig kompetanse, motivasjon og yrkesidentitet. Vi presenterer en samlet, komparativ analyse av skole og arbeidsliv som læringsarenaer på tvers av tre programområder og løfter frem et lærerperspektiv i en litteratur som primært bygger på elev- og lærlingstudier.

tittel: The Role of Science Course Pathways in Predicting College Enrollment: Insight From A Large Urban School District
kilde: Journal of Research in Science Teaching
sammendrag: ABSTRACT Although high school science course‐taking is highly valued in college admissions, its predictability for college enrollment, a key step in access to many STEM fields, has not been sufficiently investigated in the context of wide variability in science courses and updated standards. Furthermore, while ability group tracking in science has declined, tracking can persist in the levels, type, and breadth of science courses taken. The study analyzes students' science course‐taking pathways from ninth through eleventh grade and examines their relationship with college enrollment. We use cross‐classified hierarchical logistic regression modeling of students nested within both course pathways and schools in a large urban school district, examining school and course pathway features and controlling for academic performance and student characteristics. An analysis of variance partitioning shows that science course pathways explain more of the variance in on‐time college enrollment than schools. Completing the three core science courses—biology, chemistry, and physics—remains a strong predictor of college enrollment, even in the context of updated science standards, but the presence of advanced science coursework in the pathway showed the strongest association with college enrollment. Greater school STEM‐orientation was associated with increased likelihood of college enrollment.

tittel: Mentor Evaluation of a Black Male Youth Mentoring Program
sammendrag: This study was an exploration of how Black male mentors perceived organizational practices, culturally responsive mentoring, relational safety, and systems level barriers shaping their effectiveness and continued participation. The purpose was to examine early mentor-mentee match dissolution and low mentor retention in a nonprofit youth mentoring through the lens of the ecological systems theory and program evaluation framework. The practice-focused research questions were: How do volunteer mentors and program staff perceive the organizational practices and culturally responsive strategies that influence mentor effectiveness and retention in youth mentoring programs, and what organizational and systemic challenges do Black male mentors encounter in youth mentoring programs, and how do these challenges impact their sustained engagement and retention? Semi-structured interviews and focus groups with mentors and staff were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Findings were that retention improved when programs fostered relational trust, cultural responsiveness, identity affirmation, and community-rooted engagement, supported by structured training, trauma-informed practice, and consistent program fidelity. Barriers included identity-related emotional labor, limited access to supportive systems, time constraints, and burnout. Recommendations included strengthening onboarding, targeting mentor training and support, family engagement, and community partnerships. Implications for public administration included potential development of program design and practices that to reinforce mentor retention in youth programs potentially resulting in positive social change.

tittel: Impact of Private Educational Choice Policies on Traditional Public School Closures
sammendrag: Private school choice programs have expanded substantially, prompting concern that they may accelerate traditional public school closures. Using longitudinal school-level data covering 1992–2020, this study examines closure probabilities before and after choice program adoption and whether effects vary with program exposure. Event-study, linear probability, and difference-in-differences models show no evidence of abrupt increases in closures following adoption. Modest, delayed increases are concentrated in urban and town schools, while greater program intensity is not systematically associated with higher closure risk. Overall, national evidence does not support claims that private school choice broadly accelerates public school closures.

tittel: Divergent Educational Tracks and Mental Health: A Propensity Score-Matched Network Analysis of Adolescent Depression and Anxiety
sammendrag: Abstract Background Educational tracking significantly reshapes adolescent developmental ecology. The distinct psychopathological mechanisms underlying depression-anxiety comorbidity across divergent tracks remain unclear. Methods Overall, 8622 adolescents completed the PHQ-9, GAD-7, and Resilience Scale for Chinese Adolescents (RSCA). Propensity Score Matching (PSM) rigorously controlled sociodemographic variables and individual defense mechanisms to evaluate educational tracking impacts, yielding 2201 matched pairs. Gaussian Graphical Models (GGM) estimated comorbidity networks. Results Network analysis revealed a notable structural paradox. HS students maintained significantly higher symptom prevalence before and after matching. Balancing covariates rendered fundamental network topology invariant across cohorts. Matched VS students exhibited significantly higher global network strength (p < 0.001), indicating a denser, more fragile psychopathological system. Uncontrollable worry (GAD2), excessive worry (GAD3), and depressed mood (PHQ2) formed a highly conserved pathological core. A prominent somatic-arousal bridge linking psychomotor symptoms (PHQ8) and restlessness (GAD5) uniquely drove the vocational network's increased density (p = 0.004, FDR-adjusted p = 0.032). Conclusion Adolescents across tracks share a largely invariant symptom topology while exhibiting a dissociation between symptom severity and network connectivity: general students endure intense academic pressure driving elevated symptom prevalence. Vocational students confront poorer baseline protection, exhibiting a denser, more fragile comorbidity architecture. These contrasting vulnerability patterns suggest the need for dual-target systemic interventions that simultaneously alleviate excessive academic burden in general education and cultivate resilience while addressing stigma in vocational tracks.

tittel: Construction-focused alternative provision: knowledge, conduct and participation for young people at risk of educational disengagement
kilde: Journal of Vocational Education and Training
sammendrag: This study addresses a gap in research about the potential of construction alternative provision (AP) to address skills shortages within the industry and to support young people at risk of disengagement from education. Drawing on Bernstein’s theory of pedagogic discourse, this study reports the results of semi-structured interviews with nine construction AP providers across the UK, offering insights into how AP providers describe the organisation of technical skills, workplace knowledge and behavioural expectations for young people at risk of disengagement from education. The findings also show that providers associated these arrangements with greater engagement, confidence and recognition of construction as a possible occupational field. The article concludes that construction-focused AP should be understood as a diverse and under-researched form of provision that sits between general and vocational education. Rather than offering simple evidence of effectiveness, the study highlights the need for more systematic research into how construction-focused AP organises knowledge, conduct, learner identity and progression possibilities across different settings.

tittel: Putting Purpose to Work: A Qualitative Study of Purpose and Calling in Career and Technical Education and General Education High School Students
sammendrag: This qualitative descriptive study examined the purpose development and career calling of 38 ethnically diverse career and technical education (CTE; n = 13, 38.4% female, Mdnage = 17) and general education (GE; n = 25, 32% female, Mdnage = 17) purposeful high school students. The four P’s of purpose development, people, propensity, passion, and prosocial benefits guided the analysis. In-depth interviews were analyzed using directed content analysis to determine differences, if any, between CTE students and their GE counterparts on purpose development and its relationship with career calling. Key differences between CTE and GE students emerged on (1) identifying future careers as a purpose or calling that aligned with their passions; (2) purpose planning or identifying who can help them and how their purpose benefits others; and (3) living out a calling through purposeful activities or engaging in activities that build on their strengths and skills related to their purpose. These findings suggest the CTE track provides support and opportunities for purposeful students to foster and actively engage their purpose and calling in life while in school. CTE students who are purposeful may be in a unique position to both consider and live their work as a calling in life.

tittel: Estimating the Cost of Early Colleges: Three Complementary Approaches
sammendrag: Early college high schools offer students many dual enrollment courses and the opportunity to earn an associate degree while in high school. In this paper, we assess the costs of the early college model in North Carolina relative to costs for typical high school education. We use three complementary approaches: one using administrative expenditure data from high schools and colleges across the state, one using the ingredients method based on in-depth subject matter expert interviews in five case study districts, and a third “hybrid” approach combining the two methods. Our findings suggest that educating an early college student incurs higher relative costs in high school that are offset by lower costs to a college degree for students who eventually complete a postsecondary credential. However, excess credit attainment attenuates the postsecondary savings. We discuss the implications of these findings for implementation of the early college model and for cost study methodologies.

tittel: Impact of a vocational-oriented course on high school students’ knowledge, attitudes, and workplace soft skills for creative industries: a three-year study
sammendrag: Purpose A vocationally oriented course titled Multimedia Storytelling was launched in Hong Kong's mainstream high school curriculum. This study aims to evaluate the learning outcomes of the course by comparing the career readiness of enrolled and non-enrolled students as well as their knowledge of and attitudes toward the creative industries. Design/methodology/approach Three rounds of quantitative surveys were conducted among the first cohort of 105 high school students enrolled in Multimedia Storytelling from Grades 10 to 12. The same questionnaire was administered to a group of 103 non-enrolled students from the same school and grades, using convenience sampling. Findings Multimedia Storytelling students displayed higher self-ratings in knowledge of and attitude toward creative media, life and career exploration, and workplace soft skills than non-enrolled students. Among enrolled students, those in Grade 12 reported higher self-ratings in knowledge of and attitude toward creative media, workplace soft skills, and career adaptability than those in Grade 10. Research limitations/implications The research design was a repeated cross-sectional study and therefore did not allow for longitudinal comparison for the same student across different time points. Outcome measures were based on self-evaluation. There were no data to link learning outcome measures with individual components in the curriculum. Originality/value This is the first large-scale study of vocational-oriented educational outcome measures of an Applied Learning course for creative education in Hong Kong. It provides insights into curriculum design, funding, and policymaking related to vocational-oriented education at the high school level.

tittel: Formación en centros de trabajo y preparación profesional de estudiantes de Bachillerato Técnico
kilde: PsyEduca – International Journal of Educational Psychology and Guidance
sammendrag: Work-based learning connects school learning with the activities, norms, and relationships of real occupations. This scoping review mapped models applicable to Technical Baccalaureate and established criteria for assessing their contribution to professional preparation. A PRISMA-ScR review with a PCC framework was conducted, covering technical-secondary students, structured placements or alternance, and relationships among educational institutions, enterprises, and productive organizations. The final corpus comprised 16 verified sources, including international guidance, reviews, and vocational-education studies. Available evidence indicates that structured work experiences may support transitions and competence development when aligned with learning objectives, progressive activities, dual mentoring, assessment, and student protection. External placements, alternance, and Teaching Factory environments were differentiated to prevent inappropriate evidence transfer. A responsible model requires verifiable institutional agreements, an individual learning plan, coordination between mentors, performance evidence, and monitoring of equity, safety, and educational continuity. Conclusions should guide local design and inquiry rather than prescribe identical arrangements across technical programmes.

tittel: Youth Labour Market Participation in Africa: A Cross-National Analysis of Employment, Unemployment, Sectoral Distribution, and Educational Attainment Among the 15–35 Age Cohort, 2026
sammendrag: Background Africa hosts the world’s largest youth cohort, yet its labour markets remain characterised by structural imbalances, agricultural dependence, gender inequalities, and educational credential mismatches. This study provides a cross-national analysis of youth labour market participation across the 54 African Union member states in 2026, disaggregated by sex, age group, economic sector, and educational attainment. Methods A cross-sectional descriptive-correlational study was conducted using harmonised International Labour Organization (ILO) modelled estimates for youth aged 15–35 years. Youth unemployment (YUR), labour force participation (LFPR), and not-in-employment, education, or training (NEET) rates were analysed by country, sub-region, sex, age group, and education level. Pearson’s correlation assessed the association between YUR and NEET rate, while four nested ordinary least squares (OLS) models identified cross-country correlates of YUR. Results Among 545.1 million African youth, 57.1% were employed, 4.2% unemployed, 15.0% inactive, and 23.6% in education. The continental YUR was 6.91%, ranging from 0.4% in Niger to 37.4% in Eswatini, with higher unemployment in North Africa (11.09%) than sub-Saharan Africa (6.40%). The NEET rate reached 19.23%, agriculture accounted for 45.9% of youth employment, and female unemployment exceeded male unemployment (7.56% vs. 6.40%). Upper secondary and tertiary graduates represented 52.7% of unemployed youth. YUR was strongly correlated with the NEET rate (r = 0.720, p < 0.001). OLS models showed that agricultural employment share was the strongest negative correlate of YUR (β = −0.255, p < 0.001), whereas the share of educated unemployed was positively associated with YUR ( p = 0.043). Conclusions African youth labour markets exhibit substantial cross-country heterogeneity, persistent informality, and education–employment mismatches. Policies promoting structural transformation, skills alignment, gender equality, and social protection are needed. These findings highlight the limitations of unemployment rates alone as indicators of youth labour market performance.

tittel: Collaborative data dashboard design for school improvement
sammendrag: Purpose Traditional visualization approaches often fail because data scientists lack understanding of practitioner tasks, and educators lack data expertise, leading to poor tool adoption. This paper aims to offer insights from a mid-sized urban school district in the Northeastern USA, where a data dashboard designer collaborated with school administrators to develop a collective understanding of their data needs before designing visualizations. Design/methodology/approach The authors combined usage reports with data from one-on-one meetings with school principals and assistant principals, data leads and instructional leadership teams. They engaged in a qualitative case study focused on collaborative work around data dashboards, generating deductive codes based on patterns in meeting outputs and field notes. They used a Design-Based Research framework, drawing on frameworks from data visualization and human–computer interaction studies that articulate methods of data reconnaissance and task wrangling, including Crisan and Munzner (2019). Findings The outcome of this study is one example of a cycle of collaboration between researchers and practitioners, each bringing separate expertise to the data dashboard design process. By emphasizing user-voiced data needs, novel approaches to addressing equity emerged. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study serves as one of the first examples in K-12 education of a collaboratively developed set of data visualizations using user-experience and user-interface. This study uniquely focuses on school administrators, while most prior research has focused on teacher behavior. Finally, this study focuses on elementary and middle school leaders, while most data tool work has occurred within the context of high schools.

tittel: Busing to Opportunity? The Impacts of the Metco Voluntary School Desegregation Program on Urban Students of Color
sammendrag: Abstract School assignment policies are a key lever for expanding access to high-performing schools and promoting racial and socioeconomic integration. For over 50 years, the Metropolitan Council for Educational Opportunity (METCO) has bussed students of color from Boston, Massachusetts, to relatively wealthier and predominantly white suburbs. I estimate the effects of attending a high-performing suburban school by comparing applicants who receive enrollment offers with applicants who do not. A two-stage least squares approach exploits waitlist assignment priorities and controls for a rich set of characteristics from birth records and application data. Attending a suburban school boosts math and English test scores, reduces dropout, and increases on-time high school graduation. Four-year college aspirations, enrollment, and graduation increase along with earnings in adulthood. Students whose parents did not attend college and boys experience the largest effects. The evidence points to several mechanisms, including access to higher value-added schools, higher-achieving peers, and schools with stronger college-going norms. Participants are more likely to be tracked into lower-performing classes, implying that effects could be larger with access to more advanced coursework. District value-added estimates suggest that students’ educational trajectories shift at least as much as they would from growing up in the suburban districts.

tittel: Educational responsiveness to industrial upgrading: a longitudinal evaluation of higher vocational education in Shandong
kilde: International Journal of Evaluation and Research in Education (IJERE)
sammendrag: Shandong provides a concrete case for examining whether higher vocational education (HVE) can keep pace with industrial upgrading. Since the new and old kinetic energy conversion (NOKEC) strategy began in 2018, provincial policy has prioritized high-tech manufacturing and the “ten strong industries,” while HVE program structures have adjusted more slowly. This study evaluates the coordination between industrial upgrading and HVE program structure across 16 prefecture-level cities from 2016 to 2023. A dual-system indicator framework was built from official statistical yearbooks, education quality reports, and provincial bulletins. After min-max standardization, the entropy weight method (EWM), coupling coordination degree (CCD) model, and obstacle degree model were used to measure temporal evolution, spatial variation, and main constraints. The results show that coordination improved from marginal to good, but the HVE subsystem remained below the industrial subsystem throughout the period. Qingdao, Jinan, and Yantai reached high-quality coordination, while Heze remained relatively constrained. Graduate employment in strategic industries was the leading obstacle factor. The findings suggest that curriculum renewal, teacher development, enterprise co-designed modules, and graduate tracking should be strengthened to improve HVE responsiveness to regional industrial change.

tittel: Social exclusion in educational settings and the risk of alienation in adolescent development: a narrative review from a mind-body interaction perspective
sammendrag: Introduction: Social exclusion in educational settings is a salient interpersonal stressor during adolescence. However, ostracism, peer rejection, peer victimization, bullying, loneliness, and social isolation are overlapping but non-equivalent constructs. This narrative review examines how social exclusion in educational settings may contribute to the risk of alienation in adolescent development from a mind-body interaction perspective. Methods: A structured, non-exhaustive literature search was conducted in PubMed, PsycINFO, and the Web of Science Core Collection for peer-reviewed English-language publications from 1 January 2000 to 21 July 2026, supplemented by backward citation tracking. Evidence was organized by construct, population, study design, and biological level. Direct adolescent human findings were distinguished from related adolescent, adult or clinical human, and animal or cellular evidence. Results: Direct adolescent studies indicate that peer victimization and interpersonal stress can be associated with heightened peripheral cytokine reactivity, particularly among youths with additional cognitive or developmental vulnerabilities. Developmental neuroscience and neuroimmunology identify plausible endothelial, vagal, glial, synaptic, white-matter, hippocampal, and network pathways through which immune signals could interact with adolescent brain maturation. Nevertheless, the literature does not establish a continuous causal sequence from school exclusion to central neuroinflammation, altered neural plasticity, alienation, or educational impairment. Discussion: The evidence supports a conditional, evidence-graded mind-body framework rather than a deterministic pathway. Educational practice should prioritize reducing exclusion, strengthening belonging and social support, and providing accessible psychological support; general health-promoting strategies should remain complementary. Longitudinal, multimodal, and developmentally stratified studies are needed to test temporal ordering, mediation, and resilience.

tittel: IMPACT EVALUATION OF THE 'BOLSA DA MÃE' SOCIAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAM ON IMPROVING CHILDREN'S ACCESS TO EDUCATION AND HEALTH IN DILI, TIMOR LESTE
sammendrag: Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) programs have become a globally popular policy instrument for breaking the intergenerational cycle of poverty. In Timor-Leste, the 'Bolsa da Mãe' (Mother's Allowance) program was implemented with a similar objective, targeting the most vulnerable families within the nation's socio-economic structure. This study aims to quantitatively evaluate the impact of the Bolsa da Mãe program on improving access to education and health for children from beneficiary families in the urban area of Dili, a context with unique poverty dynamics. Using a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental (non-equivalent control group) design, this research compares 400 households (200 beneficiaries and 200 non-beneficiaries) matched on key socio-economic characteristics to minimize selection bias. Data was collected through in-depth structured questionnaire surveys and triangulated with secondary data from school records and health center medical records for validation. Inferential data analysis was conducted using an independent samples t-test to compare the mean achievements between the two groups. The results show that the Bolsa da Mãe program has a statistically and practically significant positive impact. The average school attendance rate for children from beneficiary families reached 94.5%, a substantial difference of 13.3 percentage points compared to 81.2% in the non-beneficiary group (p < 0.05). In terms of health, 91% of children from beneficiary families had received complete basic immunizations, far exceeding the 75% figure in the non-beneficiary group (p < 0.05). These findings indicate that Bolsa da Mãe functions not only as a social safety net that mitigates economic shocks but also as an effective human capital investment tool at the household level. The primary recommendations are for the government to strengthen compliance monitoring mechanisms digitally to enhance efficiency and to consider integrating the program with complementary services, such as nutrition education and sanitation programs, to maximize long-term impacts on human development.

tittel: PMM-based Observation as a Form of Principal Supervision in Preparing Teacher Administration and Learning Implementation to Improve Student-focused Learning
sammendrag: The principal acts as an educator who undertakes additional responsibilities, specifically managing educational units and guiding the learning process within their schools. Among the three essential competencies for principals, professional competency plays a crucial role. This includes sub-indicators related to instructional leadership—specifically in planning, implementation, assessment, and student learning outcomes—while also considering the characteristics of the teaching staff. It is essential for principals to provide mentorship to teachers as they fulfill their roles. This mentorship often involves conducting classroom observations based on PMM (Prescriptive Model of Mentoring) principles to ensure that classroom learning is optimally directed towards student engagement. The aims of this research are: (1) to develop effective instructional administration for teachers, and (2) to implement instructional strategies that prioritize student engagement. This qualitative study was conducted at SMP Negeri 3 Tulung, involving 27 teachers as participants. Data collection methods included observation, interviews, and document analysis. The data were analyzed interactively and descriptively, with validity ensured through triangulation. The key findings of this research are: (1) the development of enhanced and contextual teacher instructional administration, and (2) the implementation of engaging, student-focused instructional strategies.

tittel: The Effectiveness Of The Family Hope Program (PKH) In Reducing The Poverty Rate In Sei Bilah Village, Sei Lepan District, Langkat Regency
kilde: Journal of Management Economic and Accounting
sammendrag: This qualitative study examines the effectiveness of Indonesia's Family Hope Program (Program Keluarga Harapan/PKH), a conditional cash transfer program, in reducing poverty in Sei Bilah Village, Sei Lepan District, Langkat Regency. The research is motivated by a paradoxical phenomenon: despite a 108.1% increase in PKH recipients (from 234 to 487 beneficiary families) and an 85.2% increase in benefit amounts (from IDR 1,890,000 to IDR 3,500,000 per year) during 2015-2024, the poverty rate only decreased by 1.4 percentage points (from 14.2% to 12.8%) and has stagnated at 12.8-12.9% since 2021. This study aims to explore and understand: (1) the processes, mechanisms, and obstacles in PKH implementation; (2) beneficiary families' experiences, perceptions, and utilization patterns of assistance; and (3) the strategies and effectiveness of PKH facilitation in promoting behavioral change and economic independence. The research employs an interpretive qualitative approach. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with 12 purposively selected informants comprising 8 beneficiary families, 2 PKH facilitators, and 2 village officials, complemented by field observations and documentation studies. Data were analyzed using Miles and Huberman's interactive analysis model involving data reduction, presentation, and conclusion drawing. Data validity was ensured through source and method triangulation. The findings reveal that: (1) PKH implementation faces six structural obstacles: significant targeting errors (25-30% inclusion error due to outdated DTKS data), limited geographic access to disbursement locations imposing high transportation costs (4-5% of benefit amount), disproportionate facilitator workload (1:243-244 ratio exceeding the ideal 1:200), suboptimal inter-agency coordination for conditionality verification, limited basic service infrastructure (minimal health facilities, no senior high school, poor road conditions), and constrained facilitator authority to address structural poverty causes. PKH facilitators as street-level bureaucrats employ substantial discretion to bridge gaps between formal policies and local realities; (2) While all beneficiaries acknowledge PKH provides short-term safety net benefits, most remain skeptical about transformative impacts. Benefit utilization is dominated by basic needs consumption (70-80%), with limited allocation to education (15-20%) and productive investments (<5%). Conditionalities are perceived as fair but impose high opportunity costs; (3) Facilitation effectively increases short-term compliance with conditionalities but proves less effective in transforming long-term mindsets and fails to promote economic independence due to capacity limitations, inadequate incentives, and absence of complementary programs. This study concludes that PKH remains ineffective in reducing poverty in Sei Bilah Village due to five interrelated factors: targeting errors misallocating resources, inadequacy of benefits insufficient to fundamentally change household economic behavior, supply-side limitations in service quality and accessibility, structural poverty traps characterized by absence of formal employment opportunities preventing educated youth from escaping poverty, and limited grassroots implementation capacity. PKH functions primarily as a safety net preventing further impoverishment rather than as a springboard promoting upward economic mobility. These findings confirm street-level bureaucracy theory (Lipsky, 1980; 2010) regarding the crucial role of discretion in policy implementation, policy implementation theory (Edwards III, 1980) on the importance of communication, resources, disposition, and bureaucratic structure, and multidimensional poverty theory (Alkire & Foster, 2011; Sen, 1999) on the limitations of monetary approaches in addressing structural, multidimensional poverty. Policy recommendations include: (1) targeting system reform employing hybrid approaches combining proxy means test with community verification and more responsive data updating mechanisms; (2) benefit amount differentiation based on poverty severity and regional cost of living to ensure adequacy; (3) improved facilitator-beneficiary ratios (maximum 1:200) and enhanced facilitator incentives (minimum IDR 2-2.5 million monthly plus operational allowances); (4) PKH integration with complementary programs including skills training matching local labor market demands, microenterprise capital access, and graduation approaches facilitating transition from dependency to economic independence; (5) basic service infrastructure improvements including road rehabilitation, health facility strengthening, and senior high school establishment; and (6) local economic development creating formal employment opportunities for educated graduates through investment incentives and sector development strategies.

tittel: Evaluation of the Family Hope Program (PKH) in Agats District, Asmat Regency
sammendrag: The Family Hope Program (PKH) is a conditional cash assistance-based social protection policy aimed at reducing poverty and increasing access for poor families to education, health, and social welfare services. This study aims to evaluate the implementation of PKH in Agats District, Asmat Regency, and identify factors influencing its implementation. The study used a descriptive qualitative approach with data collection techniques through interviews, observation, and documentation. Research informants included the district head, PKH coordinator, PKH facilitator, and beneficiary families. Data were analyzed through data reduction, data presentation, and conclusion drawing, while program evaluation used William N. Dunn's six criteria, namely effectiveness, efficiency, adequacy, equity, responsiveness, and accuracy. The results show that PKH in Agats District has contributed positively to meeting the basic needs of KPM, especially in the aspects of education, maternal health, and economic support for the elderly. However, program implementation has not been fully optimal due to still facing problems with data synchronization between DTKS, Dukcapil, and Dapodik, delays in aid disbursement, limited facilitators, geographical barriers, and low understanding of some communities regarding the program mechanism. This study recommends continuous data updating, capacity building of facilitators, strengthening of cross-institutional coordination, and socio-cultural approaches to ensure more targeted implementation of PKH in remote areas.

tittel: Essays on the Public Policy of Mobility.
sammendrag: This Ph.D. thesis explores the relationship between public policy and individual mobility across space and time, with a particular focus on vulnerable populations. The three chapters aim not only to assess the effects of public policies on citizens but also to uncover the mechanisms driving these effects. Although the primary context is Brazil, the insights offered are universal. The thesis begins with an examination of historical policies, specifically the Brazilian Nationalization Campaign of the 1930s and 1940s, which sought to assimilate immigrants. It investigates how these policies influenced the human capital development of immigrants and their descendants throughout the twentieth century. The second chapter shifts to contemporary issues, analyzing the impact of poverty alleviation programs, particularly the Conditional Cash Transfer program Bolsa Família, on the social mobility of low-income households in Brazil. It tracks labor market outcomes for children who were beneficiaries in 2005 and examines their continued reliance on social programs in adulthood (2015-2019). The final chapter looks to the future, addressing the challenges posed by climate change to vulnerable populations. It investigates how social benefits, particularly the Bolsa Família program, contribute to the resilience strategies of vulnerable agricultural producers in Brazil between 2015 and 2020.

tittel: การศึกษาเปรียบเทียบปัญหาการหลุดออกนอกระบบโรงเรียนและผลกระทบ ระหว่างเทศมณฑลมอนต์เซอร์ราโด เคาน์ตี้ ประเทศไลบีเรีย และสามจังหวัดชายแดนใต้ ประเทศไทย
sammendrag: This study aims to comparatively examine the issue of school dropout and its impacts among lower secondary school students in Montserrado County, Liberia, and Thailand’s three southern border provinces. The research in Liberia employed a qualitative methodology, utilizing in-depth field interviews conducted exclusively within the country. Findings from the Liberian context reveal that prolonged and protracted armed conflict is a principal factor contributing to students' disengagement from the education system. Such disengagement has subsequently led to intergenerational poverty, as many parents, having been deprived of formal education themselves, are unable to secure stable employment or support their children's continued schooling. In contrast, the situation in Thailand’s southern border provinces was analyzed through a review of relevant literature. The findings indicate striking parallels with the Liberian case. Ongoing unrest in the region has likewise generated significant socio-economic hardship, perpetuated intergenerational poverty, and contributed to high rates of school dropout. The study offers several policy recommendations aimed at sustainably improving educational outcomes in both Montserrado County and Thailand’s three southern border provinces. These include: (1) providing financial assistance to socioeconomically vulnerable families, (2) implementing community-based awareness campaigns to elevate the perceived value of education, (3) improving school infrastructure to enhance accessibility and learning environments, and (4) formulating inclusive, equitable, and context-sensitive education policies that reflect the lived realities and specific needs of each locality.

tittel: La importancia de la mentoría social en el bienestar mocional de los menores inmigrantes y refugiados
sammendrag: Immigrants face specific stressors associated with the migratory experience and the process of adapting to a new social reality. This study assess the impact of the Nightingale project, a community-based mentoring programme whose aim is to facilitate social, cultural and linguistic cohesion of minors of immigrant origin. Analysis was carried out using a pre-test post-test design to measure the psychosocial well-being on a group of 158 young immigrants between the ages of 8 and 15. Data were statistically analysed with non-parametric tests to examine pre- to post-mentoring changes, comparing the results over a six-month period and controlling for sex and age. The analyses provide evidence of the positive impact of mentoring in specific aspects of the emotional well-being of young immigrants and highlighted the potential of this intervention method to cushion the stressful events they are subjected to in the process of settling in a new country.

tittel: Preventing Deviant Behavior Through The Implementation of an Early Warning System in Schools: A Quasi-Experimental Sociological Analysis
kilde: Central Asian Journal of Social Sciences and History
sammendrag: The article substantiates a sociological model of an early warning system aimed at the early identification of deviant behavior risk among students in general secondary schools and the organization of targeted preventive measures. The study interprets the school as an environment where the institutions of social control, socialization, and child protection intersect. The author proposes a SMART-Alert model, in which the classic ABC indicators attendance, academic performance, and behavior are supplemented with indicators of emotional state, social integration, and family engagement. The original material's aggregate indicators for 240 students, 120 in the experimental group and 120 in the control group in one school during the 2025–2026 academic year, were re-analyzed. Differences between the groups were assessed using Pearson's χ² test, relative risk, and Cramér's V coefficient. Preliminary results show that in schools where the EWS was implemented, the proportion of absenteeism, behavioral disruptions, and deviant incidents was lower, while access to psychological support and parental involvement were higher. The article substantiates the necessity of implementing the system not as a punitive monitoring tool, but as a support mechanism based on confidentiality, avoidance of stigmatization, and interagency cooperation.

tittel: PEMBENTUKAN DAN PENDAMPINGAN UNIT BIMBINGAN DAN KONSELING DI PKBM SINERGI BERDAYA SEBAGAI UPAYA PENGURANGAN ANGKA PUTUS SEKOLAH
sammendrag: Abstrak:Pendidikan nonformal melalui Pusat Kegiatan Belajar Masyarakat (PKBM) berperan penting melayani peserta didik putus sekolah, namun PKBM Sinergi Berdaya di Muara Badak, Kutai Kartanegara (192 peserta didik, 11 tutor) belum memiliki layanan Bimbingan dan Konseling (BK) yang terstruktur. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan membentuk unit BK fungsional, melatih 11 tutor sebagai konselor dasar, dan menerapkan instrumen deteksi dini peserta didik berisiko putus sekolah melalui model MoLAK Nonformal yang didukung inovasi Kursi Terapi. Kompetensi konselor dievaluasi menggunakan rubrik observasi (skala 0–100) melalui simulasi kasus pra dan pasca pelatihan; dampak program dievaluasi dari data kehadiran dan catatan putus sekolah pada buku presensi dan buku induk PKBM, dibandingkan antara periode pendampingan (Maret–Agustus 2026) dan periode enam bulan sebelumnya (September 2025–Februari 2026). Hasil menunjukkan 9 dari 11 tutor (81,8%) mencapai skor kompetensi ≥75/100 (rerata naik dari 52,4 menjadi 79,6); instrumen deteksi dini memetakan 34 dari 192 peserta didik (17,7%) berisiko, dengan 21 kasus tertangani secara internal, 9 kasus masih dalam pendampingan aktif, dan 4 kasus dirujuk ke Puskesmas/Dinas Sosial; tingkat kehadiran rata-rata meningkat dari 78% menjadi 89%; serta tidak tercatat kasus putus sekolah baru selama periode pendampingan, dibandingkan 14 kasus pada periode pembanding. Karena evaluasi ini belum menggunakan desain pembanding (kontrol), temuan tersebut merupakan indikasi awal, bukan bukti kausal, bahwa penguatan layanan BK berkontribusi terhadap kehadiran dan pencegahan putus sekolah.Abstract: Non-formal education through Community Learning Centers (PKBM) plays a vital role in serving dropout students, yet PKBM Sinergi Berdaya in Muara Badak, Kutai Kartanegara (192 students, 11 tutors) lacked a structured Guidance and Counseling (BK) unit. This service program aimed to establish a functional BK unit, train 11 tutors as basic counselors, and implement an early-detection instrument for dropout risk through the MoLAK Nonformal model supported by a Therapy Chair innovation. Counselor competency was evaluated using an observation rubric (0–100 scale) via case simulations before and after training; program impact was evaluated from attendance and dropout records in PKBM's daily logs and student roster, comparing the mentoring period (March–August 2026) with the preceding six months (September 2025–February 2026). Results (practice data) show 9 of 11 tutors (81.8%) reached a competency score ≥75/100 (mean rising from 52.4 to 79.6); the early-detection instrument identified 34 of 192 students (17.7%) as at risk, with 21 cases handled internally, 9 cases still under active mentoring, and 4 cases referred to the public health center/social service office; average attendance rose from 78% to 89%; and no new dropout case was recorded during the mentoring period, compared with 14 cases in the preceding period. As this evaluation did not use a comparison (control) design, these findings are an early indication, not causal evidence, that strengthening BK services contributes to attendance and dropout prevention.

tittel: Finding the Balance: State Fiscal Sustainability and Local Government Fiscal Challenge
kilde: Illinois Digital Environment for Access to Learning and Scholarship (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign)
sammendrag: The end of Illinois’ 2023 fiscal year marked the completion of the first year after which the state government fully allocated the State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (SLFRF) from the COVID pandemic. In previous reports (see Wilbur-Mujtaba et. al. 2023 and past reports at https://igpa.uillinois.edu/tag/fiscal-futures), our team at the Fiscal Futures Project has cautioned that Illinois’s fiscal situation remains challenging amidst the end of pandemic federal relief funds, and that lawmakers must continue to monitor spending closely to assure alignment with revenue. In this report, we provide an update on Illinois’s current fiscal situation by examining state governmental revenue and expenditures during FY2023. In addition, we outline the major fiscal challenges of Illinois’ local governments, from mass transit issues to changes in the commercial property market and property tax burdens. After reviewing the issues across Illinois’s local governments, we conclude with implications for state government finance in Illinois. In summary, Illinois’ fiscal condition is surely stronger than it was prior to the pandemic and, in fact, stronger than it has been over most of the last two decades. Significant challenges remain. In our view, Illinois state finances have become the most sustainable since the project began tracking budget data. Despite this, current revenue policy may not be sufficient to sustain expected long-term expenditure growth, and we see few large categories of expenditures that will be easy to restrain. In past years, Illinois’ fiscal situation has forced lawmakers to juggle programs when they are not able to achieve long-term objectives. Prominent examples include public workers’ pension policies and education finance. For many years, Illinois’ pension payments were insufficient to pay for benefits accrued by state employees. These policies eventually resulted in the introduction of relatively meager Tier 2 pensions for new workers, in order to subsidize the retirement of long-term Tier 1 employees (see Merriman 2011; Dye, Hudspeth and Merriman, 2014).

tittel: An evaluation of a profiling and selection process for apprentices in the South African automotive industry
sammendrag: The South African automotive industry is the biggest manufacturing sector and the largest contributor to the domestic economy. Within the national manufacturing sector, the artisan job family has been identified as a scarce and critical skill. Artisans are a number one area of concern with regard to filling vacancies in the country. The domestic economy as well as the effectiveness and success of the automotive industry could be negatively affected if this artisanal crisis is not adequately addressed. This study aimed to evaluate a profiling and selection process for apprentices in the South African automotive industry. A multiple-stage selection method was used to screen the applicants. The selection process included the following phases: application review, rating of the application documentation, aptitude testing, skills-based teamwork assessment and interviews. The researcher obtained access to the documentation generated through an annual apprentice selection process at a large multi-national automotive firm. The final sample consisted of 3 412 individuals that had applied for two types of apprenticeship programmes, namely, automotive electrician and millwright, across three intake years. Descriptive statistics such as frequency distribution tables and medians were used. Inferential statistical analysis, using survival analysis, was used to assess whether the survival curves were statistically different across the groups. The findings of this study are relevant to the South African automotive industry, as well as the manufacturing sector. The findings are also of value to human resource practitioners, educators, social scientists and other researchers. The 13 constructs investigated in the study showed a high association with longer survival time in the selection process. The positive evaluation of this selection process provides evidence to support its confirmation as the national selection tool. Four recommendations are proposed to the HRM field and four to the automotive industry. The multiple-hurdle selection process employed in this study should be replicated by the automotive industry in their selection of apprenticeship applicants. Standardisation practices, the use of on-line technology and the marketing of the apprenticeship position are also recommended. Furthermore, it is recommended that educational providers provide job preparation workshops to assist applicants to improve their survival opportunity within the selection processes.

tittel: I Was There, I Belonged There, and I Should Be There: The Adult Student Experience in Community College Courses Filled With High School Students
sammendrag: The rapid expansion of dual-enrollment and early college high school programs in North Carolina has led to a substantial increase in the numbers of dual-enrolled high school students in community college classrooms. This exploratory case study examined how adult students described their experiences in university-transfer courses in which dual-enrolled high school students make up the majority of the class. It also examined how some of these adult students’ instructors described the experiences of these adult students. The current study was conducted at three community colleges in rural counties in southern Appalachia and included semi-structured interviews with 18 adult students (24-60 years) and two focus-group interviews with nine instructors who taught their university-transfer courses. Descriptive and pattern coding was used to identify seven themes across participant responses: • Adult students know they belong, even if they do not always feel they belong. • Adult students’ sense of belonging may grow through the semester. • Classes with dual-enrolled students do not harm adult student progress. • Many adult students engage as leaders in classes with high school students. • Instructors prefer classes with a mixture of student ages. • Instructors’ understanding of student belonging and teaching styles were linked. • Instructors do not assign special responsibilities to adult students. This study finds that adult students are an asset in multigenerational classrooms and that instructors play a critical role in shaping student connection and adult students’ sense of belonging. Implications are provided for policymakers, community college leaders, and instructors seeking to support student belonging and success in age-diverse learning environments.

tittel: The Role of High School Leaders in Advancing College and Career Readiness for Students Classified as English Learners
sammendrag: Abstract As attention has grown to expanding “college and career readiness” (CCR) for students classified as English Learners (ELs) in U.S. schools, an understudied piece of the puzzle is the role of high school leaders. Given their responsibilities for overseeing curriculum and instruction and implementing state and district policies, site leaders have outsized influence on ELs' access to CCR pathways. This paper reports on a two‐case study, using ethnographic methods, that explored the ways site leaders in two comprehensive high schools navigated language policy and other institutional factors with consequences for access to CCR for ELs. The study found that while the school leaders voiced commitment to equitable outcomes for ELs and assets‐oriented views of students' developing bilingualism, they encountered dilemmas in working to ensure that ELs received the specialized language instruction they needed and were fully included in the range of CCR opportunities their schools offered. In response to these dilemmas, school leaders prioritized certain policies and goals over others and attempted to leverage schoolwide structures to address multiple goals. Our findings have implications for language education research as well as policymakers and school leaders seeking to maximize postsecondary pathways for ELs.

tittel: Assessing the Effect of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) on Household Income: A Case Study of Pul-e-Khumri, Afghani
kilde: Kunduz University International Journal of Islamic Studies and Social Sciences
sammendrag: Vocational training provides practical and skill-based learning that enables individuals to acquire competencies relevant to labor market requirements. This study examined the effect of vocational training on household income in Pul-e-Khumri District, Baghlan Province. The study population comprised 980 individuals who had completed vocational training programs. Based on Morgan’s sampling table, 280 participants were selected using convenience sampling. Data were collected through a researcher-developed questionnaire employing a five-point Likert scale ranging from very high to very low. The instrument demonstrated satisfactory reliability, with a Cronbach’s alpha coefficient of 0.882. Its validity was established through the expert judgments of three scholars specializing in Social Sciences, Mathematics, and Dari Language and Literature. Descriptive findings revealed that 23.2% of respondents held a bachelor’s degree, while most had a diploma or lower qualification. Tailoring was the most common vocational skill (20.7%), followed by mobile-phone repair (19.3%), plastering and metalwork (12.5% each), solar installation (12.1%), and furnituremaking and carpentry (11.4% each). Overall, 72.1% of participants obtained employment after completing their training. CFA and SEM analyses showed that vocational training significantly improved household income through both direct and indirect pathways, particularly by strengthening occupational skills, attitudes, goal orientation, and employment opportunities. All hypotheses were supported. The findings indicate that expanding vocational training can be an effective approach to promoting employment and strengthening household livelihoods

tittel: An Unconventional Path to Universal School Choice: Oklahoma’s Parental Choice Tax Credit Program
sammendrag: A major concern with universal private school choice programs is that they will reduce funding for public schools. This article explores the adoption of Oklahoma’s universal private school choice legislation – the Parental Choice Tax Credit (PCTC) program. Oklahoma’s case is instructive because it demonstrates how the political compromises needed to pass universal private school choice legislation produced a historic increase in recurring funding for public schools despite claims that the program would have the opposite effect. Oklahoma’s law also structurally linked funding streams so that if public education funding declined, then funds for private school choice would be reduced.

tittel: Mentoring Relationship Quality: An Evaluation of Environmental Risk and Protective Factor Predictors for Urban Black Youth
sammendrag: Mentoring programs are an important intervention promoting positive developmental outcomes among youth exposed to chronic environmental stressors, particularly Black youth living in underinvested communities. Research has demonstrated moderate positive effects of mentoring on youth outcomes however, less is known about factors influencing mentoring effectiveness. Mentoring relationship quality (MRQ) has emerged as a key component of mentoring effectiveness, suggesting that perceived closeness and support within the relationship can enhance youth outcomes. Less is known regarding the environmental risks and protective factors shaping youths’ ability to engage meaningfully in mentoring relationships. Parent–child relationship quality, exposure to violent stressors, and adaptive and maladaptive coping strategies may influence mentoring experiences, though findings remain mixed. The present study sought to examine whether parent–child relationship quality, exposure to violent stressors, and coping strategies at baseline, subsequently predicted MRQ. This study examined whether parent–child relationship quality and coping strategies moderated the relationship between exposure to violent stressors and MRQ. Participants included 81 youth in a mentoring intervention. Findings indicated that parent–child relationship quality was positively associated with MRQ, and female mentees consistently reported stronger MRQ across analyses. Exposure to violent stressors and coping strategies did not significantly predict MRQ, although correlational findings suggest indirect pathways, linking violent stress exposure, coping responses, and relational experiences. No significant moderation effects emerged. Findings suggest MRQ may be shaped less by specific risk or protective factors alone and more through indirect relational and contextual processes. Implications for culturally responsive mentoring interventions and future mentoring research are discussed.

tittel: A QUANTITATIVE STUDY ON THE IMPACT OF ALTERNATIVE EDUCATION PLACEMENTS ON GRADUATION OUTCOMES OF PUBLIC EDUCATION STUDENTS IN SPECIAL POPULATIONS
kilde: Index of Texas Archaeology Open Access Grey Literature from the Lone Star State
sammendrag: ABSTRACT This study examined the relationship between Disciplinary Alternative Education Program (DAEP) placement and graduation outcomes among students in special populations within a large, urban public school district in Texas. Grounded in Social Cognitive Theory, this study analyzed a four-year longitudinal cohort to determine whether DAEP placement was associated with differences in graduation outcomes, including on-time graduation, late graduation, and dropout status. The study examined differences between students with single and multiple DAEP placements. The sample included over 4,000 students including students who experienced DAEP placement. Data were analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics to compare outcomes between DAEP and non-DAEP students. Results indicated that DAEP placement was associated with lower rates of on-time graduation and higher rates of delayed graduation or dropouts. No statistically significant difference was found between students with single and multiple DAEP placements, suggesting a cumulative impact. Findings highlight the need for targeted interventions, improved reintegration practices, and policy considerations to better support students in alternative education settings. Keywords: Disciplinary Alternative Education Program (DAEP), Alternative Education Program (AEP), graduation outcomes, special populations, alternative education, student discipline, longitudinal study, educational leadership

tittel: Effects of unconditional cash transfers on financial inclusion: evidence from rural Northern Uganda
sammendrag: Scepticism and hope surround debates about the effectiveness of unconditional cash transfers (UCTs), yet evidence remains inadequate. While existing research has largely examined effects of transitioning from cash to digital transfers, we examine the effects of UCTs in rural Northern Uganda on financial inclusion outcomes beyond the delivery channel. Using Propensity Score Matching, we found that regular monthly UCTs had significant positive effects on access to and use of formal and informal financial services, most pronounced among the women who also received children’s transfers. The formal financial inclusion effects were largest on mobile money, followed by non-deposit-taking and deposit-taking financial institutions. The magnitude of effects on informal financial arrangements was comparable to mobile money, reflecting their significance. We recommend leveraging mobile money and informal financial arrangements to integrate UCTs with financial inclusion initiatives. Future research should use larger, longitudinal, and comparative approaches to examine the intensive-margin and sustainability of effects.

tittel: A Causal-Comparative Study of Self-Efficacy in Certificate and Degree Programs at the Community College Level Upon Graduation
sammendrag: This quantitative causal-comparative study investigated whether student-perceived occupational self-efficacy differs between graduates of community college certificate programs and those completing Associate of Applied Science (AAS) degrees. The research also addresses a gap in the literature regarding how award type influences occupational self-efficacy among students in automotive, diesel, manufacturing, and welding programs. The study employed a causal-comparative research design, examining the relationship between the categorical independent variable of award type (certificate or AAS degree) and the quantitative dependent variable of occupational self-efficacy. Participants (N=209) were students in their graduating term from community colleges in a Northwestern state who were completing one of the target programs. Data was collected using the Occupational Self-Efficacy Scale (OSES). Descriptive statistics summarize demographic and study variables, including means, standard deviations, frequencies, and percentages. A two-way ANOVA tested for statistically significant differences and found no significant interaction or main effects between the award types or the disciplines on occupational self-efficacy. The findings of this study expand the literature on occupational self-efficacy at the community college level with technical graduates and offer insights that can support program development and leadership decision-making. This research serves as a foundation for future studies exploring the nuances of student self-efficacy post-graduation. Future research should assess data through longitudinal study methodology and incorporate a mixed-method approach among a different population compared with a different instrument.

tittel: Changing Course: Robots and Human Capital Investment in High School
sammendrag: We study how industrial robots affect human capital investment during high school. Using Texas administrative records and an instrument based on European robot adoption, we find that exposure reduces dropout, raises observed completion, and shifts coursework toward college preparation and away from vocational subjects. Advanced coursework increases across grades, while dropout reductions and gains in quantitative coursework are concentrated in upper grades. Boys reduce vocational coursework more, narrowing gender differences in course taking, whereas girls increase advanced coursework more, widening their advantage in college preparation. Adjustment to automation is already underway in high school, through continued schooling and curricular choices.

tittel: The Supply of Expertise: New Technologies, New Skills, and Worker Impacts
sammendrag: Does educational content respond to technological advances, and do such changes enable workers to acquire new valuable expertise? We construct a novel database of legally binding training curricula spanning the near universe of vocational training in Germany over five decades, and link curriculum updates to breakthrough technologies using Natural Language Processing. We trace a causal chain from technological change to curriculum content to worker outcomes. Technological change spurs curriculum updates, and training content shifts toward less routine-intensive tasks. This shift occurs predominantly through the emergence of new skills related to social, digital, and problem-solving competencies, rather than the removal of old ones. This within-occupation margin is quantitatively important: curriculum updates account for two-thirds of the overall deroutinization in vocational skill supply over this period. Using administrative employer-employee data and a stacked difference-in-differences design, we show that new-skilled workers earn higher wages, especially in technology-exposed occupations, and are more likely to remain employed in their trained occupation. In contrast, older occupational incumbents experience wage declines, indicating skill obsolescence. These findings highlight the central role of within-occupation skill supply adjustments — not just educational attainment — in meeting evolving labor market demands.

tittel: A narrative inquiry on student perception of failing Algebra 1 and participation in subsequent high school mathematics courses
sammendrag: Algebra 1 is significant within a student's high school mathematics coursework.Initial failure of Algebra 1 can have a continued impact on a student's subsequent mathematics coursework since prior research indicates students who fail Algebra 1 do not achieve the same level of mathematical competencies as students who initially pass.Research on the failure of students in Algebra 1 is largely quantitative; significant qualitative inquiry on the topic is lacking.Thus, the purpose of this qualitative study was to investigate how students who fail Algebra 1 describe their experience in Algebra 1 and their experiences in the subsequent years of high school mathematics coursework.This study approached the topic through a narrative inquiry methodology.Six participants who failed Algebra 1 but ultimately graduated from high school were interviewed, and the interview transcripts were analyzed using codes, categories, and patterns to identify themes.The findings were expressed through six core narratives, each an amalgamation of participant experiences.Core narratives and subsequent discussions on narratives focused on the themes of peer comparison, belongingness, social norms, studentteacher relationships, teacher commitment, and student-responsive instruction.Cross-narrative themes of engagement and perception emerged.The lasting impact of an initial negative Algebra 1 experience and the significant effect of participant feelings were addressed.The goal-oriented nature of positive experiences and the external attribution of negative experiences were also addressed.The findings of this study may be useful to teachers, school counselors, intervention specialists, curriculum leaders, teacher educators, administrators, and policymakers wanting to develop learning environments and educational practices that better support students who experience academic challenges and setbacks.The results of this study have potential impacts on school policy and classroom student support.Recommendations include the creation of a policy addressing subsequent course enrollment following failure of Algebra 1 and the creation of a standard response protocol for initiating support for students who fail Algebra 1. Classroom recommendations include establishing a classroom culture defined by social safety, psychological safety, and active engagement, and intentionally creating a student-teacher relationship characterized by both positive social and academic interactions.

tittel: The Relationship Between Earning Dual Enrollment Credits and Saving Time and Money in Undergraduate Degree Completion at a Christian College
kilde: Journal of Research on Christian Education
sammendrag: Dual enrollment programs are billed as valuable preparation for success in college and often promote opportunities for reduced time and expense in college-degree completion. However, there appears to be a lack of research actually supporting, or disproving, these claims of profitability. This research used a quantitative, correlational study to evaluate the predictive relationship between the number of dual enrollment credits earned by students while in high school and the subsequent length of time to college degree completion. The sample included 103 undergraduate students pursuing a baccalaureate degree at Midwestern, private, nonprofit, religious university. Utilizing self-reported demographic data and measures derived through the Graduating Student Survey (GSS), a multiple regression analysis revealed no statistically significant relationship based on the linear combination of dual enrollment credits, anticipated college debt load, and time to degree completion. Limitations of the study include a non-diverse sampling and the use of self-reported data. Implications and recommendations for future research are provided. The authors report there are no competing interests to declare.

tittel: The Impact of a Peer-to-Peer Mentoring Program on University Choices and Performance
Modern Concepts of Higher and Professional Education Integration in Providing Qualified Personnel for Regional Economic Sectors
kilde: American Journal of Economics and Business Management
sammendrag: The article systematizes modern conceptual approaches to the integration of higher and professional education in providing regional economic sectors with qualified personnel. The economic content of the concepts of the skills ecosystem, skills needs anticipation, lifelong learning and flexible educational trajectories, competency-based education, dual and work-based learning, the regional innovation ecosystem, and digital analytics of skills is revealed. Their role in coordinating the demand and supply of personnel in the regional labour market, increasing the alignment of educational programmes with sectoral specialization, and strengthening the efficiency of human-capital utilization is substantiated. As the author's own approach, it is proposed to organize the integration of higher and professional education around the chain “forecasting regional demand – competency mapping – integrated educational trajectory – joint training with the employer – outcome monitoring.”

tittel: Unconditional Cash Transfers, Women’s Empowerment and the Use of Maternal Healthcare: Evidence from BISP Beneficiaries in Multan Division, Pakistan
sammendrag: Pakistan’s maternal mortality ratio remains well above the Sustainable Development Goal target, and much of the shortfall is linked to women’s limited ability to decide on, pay for and travel to care. This study examined whether receipt of the Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), an unconditional cash transfer paid to women, and women’s multidimensional empowerment were associated with the use of antenatal care, skilled birth attendance and postnatal care. Primary data were collected from 768 ever-married women in the four districts of Multan Division, Punjab, split equally between BISP beneficiaries and locality-matched non-beneficiaries. Economic, social, familial and political empowerment indices, together with an overall index, were constructed through Principal Component Analysis from 31 survey items. Because women’s empowerment is plausibly endogenous, instrumental-variable probit models were estimated with women’s house ownership and land ownership as two instruments and each empowerment index entered in a separate model, for the pooled division and separately for each district. BISP receipt was positively associated with all three maternal care outcomes; the average marginal effect was largest for skilled birth attendance. Economic empowerment was the strongest single empowerment dimension, political empowerment the weakest, and familial empowerment was only weakly and inconsistently associated with care. The interactions of BISP with the economic, social and overall empowerment indices were positive and mostly significant, pointing to complementarity between cash and women’s bargaining power; the interactions with familial and political empowerment were largely insignificant. The cost of visits and distance to a facility were the largest barriers, while television was the information channel most strongly associated with care. Associations were strongest in Multan district and weakest in Lodhran. The findings supported protecting BISP coverage while pairing it with economic empowerment, transport and fee support, and district-targeted health infrastructure.

tittel: Bundling a conditional cash transfer program with an inclusive life insurance policy: an exploratory analysis of the female beneficiaries of the Brazilian “Programa Bolsa Família”
kilde: The Geneva Papers on Risk and Insurance Issues and Practice

tittel: From Compliance to Continuous Improvement: Applying Institutional Research and Accreditation Practices to Secondary Education
sammendrag: This chapter examines how institutional research (IR), assessment, and accreditation practices can support continuous improvement in secondary education when adapted from higher education with attention to context. It argues that federal reporting systems, dashboards, and artificial intelligence (AI) can make evidence more visible, but visibility alone does not improve learning. Improvement depends on whether schools and postsecondary partners define outcomes clearly, align curricula, protect student data, interpret results within context, and act on what they learn. The chapter situates this work within the policy infrastructure created by the Every Student Succeeds Act (ESSA), state and local report cards, Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS) reporting, Title IV eligibility, and federal recognition of accrediting agencies. It also considers how secondary accreditation and postsecondary accreditation share a common quality assurance logic, even though they operate in different institutional settings. Building from scholarship on continuous improvement, data use, assessment, and learning analytics, the chapter presents an evidence-to-improvement cycle for the secondary-to-postsecondary continuum. The framework emphasizes data governance, stakeholder interpretation, early warning indicators, curriculum alignment, analytics, and human judgment as essential conditions for meaningful and sustainable improvement. The chapter ultimately argues that compliance provides a necessary foundation, but improvement occurs only when evidence is connected to decisions, resources, and changes in educational practice.

tittel: Fostering Connections: How Mentoring Relationships Can Promote Youth Social Capital
sammendrag: Little is known about how mentors support mentees in strengthening social capital. It is theorized that mentors support mentees in building new connections and strengthening existing relationships (i.e., connection-building support). This mixed-methods study examines how connection-building support contributes to mentee's network mobilization in pursuit of life goals. Survey data were gathered from youth (n = 122) ages 13-18 (88% youth of color; 57% female). A path model tested the association between connection-building support and mentee goal attainment and occupational identity via network mobilization. Interviews with 12 mentor-mentee pairs further elucidated how mentors support mentee social capital. Connection-building support was indirectly associated with greater progress toward life goals and stronger occupational identity via network mobilization. Qualitative findings added nuance on mentor actions that support mentee social capital. Findings highlight implications for practice and offer considerations for strengthening youth social capital in mentoring relationships.

tittel: “Long Term Labor Market Consequences of Keeping Girls in School: Evidence from a Conditional Cash Transfer in India
sammendrag: Abstract Gendered socio-cultural norms resulting in institutionalization of gendered specializations in home production is a leading cause for low and stagnant female labor force participation rates in developing countries. This paper examines a unique Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) program for education of girls implemented in the Indian state of West Bengal in 2013. Though the primary objective of the program was to keep girls in schools, we explore if such a demand-side intervention affects long run labor market outcomes. Exploiting cohort specific eligibility rules and timing of program implementation, we employ a quasi-experimental empirical framework to find that urban women exposed to this program are 4.6 percentage points more likely to be employed as a salaried or regular-wage worker. We also find a 3.0 percentage points increase in women being available for work.
